# THE GOLDEN FLEECE <note>original Latin: "Aureum Vellus"</note>
->or<-
## Golden Treasure and Cabinet of Art:

**I**n which the writings and books of the most distinguished, excellent, chosen, magnificent, and proven authors [are contained], drawn from the ancient, long-surviving, hidden, and withheld relics and monuments of the Egyptian, Arabian, Chaldean, and Assyrian kings and sages.
->By<-
**T**he noble, highly enlightened, and excellent philosopher Trismosinos (who was the teacher <note>original Latin: "Preceptor"</note> of the great philosopher and physician Theophrastus Paracelsus), arranged into distinct and separate little treatises and translated into German.
**T**his, together with other separate treatises by ancient and modern philosophical writers, all never before seen in print, as the catalog <note>original Latin: "Catalogus"</note> shows.
**B**rought together through a lover of the arts with great expense, toil, labor, and danger from the original documents and manuscripts, and published with the greatest faithfulness and diligence.
**P**rinted at Rorschach on Lake Constance.
**I**n the year 1598.

<summary>This title page introduces a famous alchemical compendium attributed to Solomon Trismosinos, claiming to be a collection of secret ancient wisdom and the source of Paracelsus's knowledge.</summary>

# Treatise and Wandering
## Of the Highly Renowned Lord Salomon
## Trismorinus <note>Salomon Trismosin is a legendary alchemist, famously cited as the teacher of the great physician Paracelsus. His "Wandering" describes a quest for the Philosopher's Stone.</note> Together with Three
## Powerful Tinctures.

When I was a journeyman, I came to a villager named Pfeiffer, who was also a practitioner of the alchemical arts; but he kept all his affairs hidden, and I could get nothing from him. He had a piece of common lead <term>Saturn (♄): the alchemical name and symbol for lead, associated with the slow-moving planet Saturn.</term> and a powder or salt for it. He fixed the lead <note>original: "♄"</note> so long until it became fixed and fluid, and afterwards like wax. Of this prepared lead <note>original: "♄"</note>, along with 20 *lot* <note>A German unit of weight; 20 lot is approximately 10 ounces.</note> and 1 mark <note>A mark was a traditional weight for precious metals, roughly 8 ounces.</note> of fine silver <term>Luna (☾): the alchemical name and symbol for silver, associated with the Moon.</term> that contained shining gold <term>Sol (☉): the alchemical name and symbol for gold, associated with the Sun.</term>, he let both [undergo the process] <note>original: "m: o: a:", likely standing for "mit ordentlicher Arbeit," meaning "with the proper procedure."</note> in half an hour. Afterwards, Pfeiffer cast it into an ingot; the work was half gold <note>original: "☉"</note>. My heart rejoiced greatly that I should have service to this art, and I thought I would ask him about it, but it was refused me. Not long after, he fell into a worry <note>Likely a euphemism for a terminal illness or legal trouble.</note> and no one could learn of his <insert>Art</insert> before he departed. Because I saw this truth myself with this villager, I set out on my way in the year 1472 <note>original: "M. CCCC. LXXJJ"</note> and traveled here and there. Wherever I heard of an artist, I was diligent to go to him. And I spent a year and a half in this wandering, and learned all kinds of arts from alchemy which do not bring much benefit. There I recognized the truth in several particulars <term>Particulars: alchemical results that successfully transform a small amount of metal but cannot be scaled up or used to create the "Universal" Philosopher's Stone.</term> and consumed 200 florins, yet I did not think of giving up.

I intended and was diligent that I and my friends raised traveling money, and I took my journey with a strange man from Ljubljana <note>original: "Labach"</note>, from there to Milan, and came into a monastery. There I served as an assistant and heard his lessons for a year. Afterwards, I traveled all over Italy <note>original: "Welchsland"</note> and came to an Italian merchant and a Jew who knew German. These mastered the art of "clothing" the English mercury <term>Mercurius (☿): the alchemical name and symbol for quicksilver.</term>—how that cost [E.?] <note>The letter "E" here may be a shorthand for a price or a specific chemical grade.</note>, they kept hidden, which I will omit. He asked me for my service as a helper <note>original: "Zülions," likely from the term for a scullion or low-ranking kitchen/lab servant.</note>, if it was pleasing to him; the Jew persuaded the merchant that he should take me as a servant. And I had to do the sulfur <term>Sulfur (🜍): along with Mercury and Salt, one of the three primary principles of alchemy.</term> work when they made their art with tin <term>Jupiter (♃): the alchemical name and symbol for tin.</term>. I was diligent

### Treatise on the Wandering

And he <note>Referring to a new unnamed master mentioned at the end of the previous page.</note> liked me well, and therefore kept nothing hidden from me; thus I also learned the art, which involved poisonous things <note>Likely referring to arsenic, mercury, or other volatile minerals used in alchemical "multiplication."</note>. I remained with him for 14 weeks.

Afterwards, I traveled with the Jew <note>The text refers to his companion by his religion, a common practice in 16th-century travelogues; this individual was likely a merchant or fellow alchemist.</note> to Venice, where he sold to a Turkish merchant about 40 pounds <note>original: "ł"</note> of <term>Mercury (☿)</term>. While he was bargaining with the merchant, I took 6 lot <note>A German weight unit; 6 lot is roughly 3 ounces.</note> of the <term>Mercury (☿)</term> and went to a goldsmith. He had two journeymen who spoke Latin <note>original: "Lateinisch"</note>; I requested that he should test this <term>Mercury (☿)</term> for me. Thereupon, he directed me across St. Mark’s Square to an assayer <note>A specialist who tests the purity of precious metals.</note> who was very stately and wealthy. He had three Italian <note>original: "welssche," a term used for Romance-language speakers, particularly Italians.</note> assayer-journeys, who sought to test such a "web" <note>original: "gespinnst," likely referring to the chemical composition or the "spun" appearance of the treated metal.</note> with very sharp things <note>Likely strong acids like aqua fortis.</note>, and afterwards they refined it by cupellation <note>original: "triebens... ab," the process of heating ore to separate noble metals from base metals.</note> on the "horse" <note>original: "roß," possibly a technical term for a specific type of furnace support or cupel bench.</note>. 

But it failed and stood up to no test at all; everything flew away in the <term>Fire (△)</term>. And they spoke to me harshly, asking where I had obtained this <term>Mercury (☿)</term>. I testified that I had only had it tested so that I might see what kind of good <term>Mercury (☿)</term> it was.

When I saw that it was false, I went no more to the Jew, and I valued this art <note>The deceptive method of his previous master.</note> no longer, for I thought I might fall into misfortune because of the Jew and the false <term>Mercury (☿)</term>. And afterwards I found myself there in Venice in a lodging and a charitable house <note>original: "hüll. Und Casse," likely referring to a shelter or a "Casa" (house) of a religious order.</note> where I had food twice a day. There the Rector had me directed to a hospital <note>In this context, a "Spital" was a hostel for travelers and the needy, not just the sick.</note>; there were other Germans inside as well, and they gave stately food there. It was for all nations and fellowship. 

The next day, I went to St. Mark’s Square, where one of the assayer-journeymen who had previously tested the <term>Mercury (☿)</term> came to me. He addressed me, asking if I had any more of that <term>Mercury (☿)</term>. I said no, but that I possessed the art: namely, how the <term>Mercury (☿)</term> was made, and I would gladly share it with him. This pleased the assayer well, and he asked if I could also perform other alchemical labors <note>original: "Laborieren," meaning practical laboratory work.</note>. I said yes, quite a bit. Then he said that if I were willing, there was a nobleman <note>original: "Centilon," likely a corruption of the Italian "Gentiluomo" (Gentleman).</note> here who favored alchemical laboring greatly, and had long wished to have a German laboratory assistant. 

It pleased me, and he led me straight to the head assistant, who was a German named Hans Stauber. And how lucky! <note>original: "wandter!" an exclamation of good fortune or a "turn" of fate.</note> He took me on immediately and gave me 2 crowns every week, plus food. Then he led me about 16 miles from Venice to a great house belonging to that same lord, which he called Pantilon <note>Possibly a corruption of a name like "Pantaleone" or a specific villa name.</note>.

### The Experiments of Salomon Trismosin

I have never in my life seen such alchemical work, nor such various specific tinctures <note>A "particular" tincture was an alchemical substance meant to transform a specific base metal into a precious one, unlike the "universal" Philosopher’s Stone.</note>; everything one could possibly imagine was in stock in that place. Each laborer (of whom there were twelve) had his own chamber, and they all had their own cooks. There, the head alchemist gave me a piece in my hand that had been brought to Centilon for 4 gold coins; it was a coagulation of <term>Mercury (☿)</term> <note>The process of "freezing" or solidifying liquid mercury into a solid state.</note>. The head alchemist mixed it for me so that I would not recognize it, and I had to work that piece out to the end. This took 12 hours <note>original: "s.", likely *stunden* (hours)</note>. I was diligent, and the "particular" transmutation succeeded well for me. When the coagulation was tested and separated at 19 lot <note>A German weight unit; 19 lot is approximately 10 ounces.</note>, 31 lot of the best <term>Gold (☉)</term> resulted. That was my first work and success.

The head alchemist immediately reported this to Centilon, who came out to me in an incomprehensible state <note>This may refer to the Count being overwhelmed with excitement or the difficulty of their communication.</note>. He spoke to me in Latin <note>original: "Latinisch"</note> and called me "The Fortunate One" <note>original: "Fortunatum"</note>. He was not perfect in Latin; he tapped me on the shoulder, but I did not understand him well as his speech was entirely corrupt <note>meaning he spoke "broken" or grammatically incorrect Latin.</note>. He presented me with 29 crowns <note>A common gold coin of the era.</note>. At that time, I was strictly bound by an oath of life and limb that everything must be kept secret, which was only fair. And I said: "If anyone, like myself, should come upon this art and strike the truth, then by the eternal justice of God, he must not let such art spread further. Therefore, hold your tongue <note>original: "halt ds Maul," literally "hold the muzzle," a very blunt command for silence.</note>; even if you possess the highest tincture, give of it to the poor."

I saw that I could observe all kinds of arts with this Centilon, as the head alchemist was very loyal to me and shared all sorts of techniques and handiwork. He also informed me that his gracious master spent 30,000 crowns a year on such arts, paying for all kinds of books brought to him in every language, and giving great rewards for them. I myself truly saw a Parlamathan <note>Likely a proper name or a title of a foreign traveler.</note> bring a tincture treatise in the Greek language <note>original: "griechischer sprach"</note> from other lands...

...was brought, for which 6,000 Crowns <note>A significant sum of gold currency.</note> were given to him. Centilon was so magnificent and powerful. All of these possessed a great treasure of the **Tincture**. It is a marvel that the Eternal Divinity revealed such things to the heathens, though they lived in ancient times.

# Lord Salomon Trismosin’s 4th Treatise

After I had spent a short time there and saw the true foundation of this Art, I began to work on the best Tincture <note>The alchemical substance used to transform base metals into gold or silver.</note>. There are about seven excellent varieties, yet all of them grow from a single root. When I attained this Art, I found such a beautiful redness that no pearls could compare to it. Truly, after the process of augmentation <term>augmentation: increasing the power or quantity of the alchemical medicine</term>, I used one part to transform 1,000 parts of metal into the finest **Gold** <term>☉</term>. I also took **Silver** <term>☽</term>, **Mercury** <term>☿</term>, and **Lead** <term>♄</term>, along with **Iron** <term>♂</term>, **Copper** <term>♀</term>, **Gold** <term>☉</term>, and **Tin** <term>♃</term>, brought them to a ringing melt, and cast the Tincture upon them. It all became the healthiest gold. I will not write now of the vast number of hundredweights and other metals I tinted after manifold multiplication <term>multiplication: the process of intensifying the Tincture's transformative power</term>, at which I myself was amazed.

But whoever wishes to deal with such a great matter should pray diligently, thank and honor God, give alms to the poor, and show themselves to be a faithful help to their neighbors. Refrain from evil vices, and then great fortune will visibly appear through these secrets, more than you would ever expect.

## Trismosin

The true Red Lot <note>The "Red Lot" or Red Tincture represents the final, most perfect stage of the alchemical work (the Rubedo).</note> is not to be revealed. I even commanded my disciples in the East and in Hungary to inquire after it, for its origin is initially not from **Gold** <term>☉</term>. However, the **Gold** <term>☉</term> is "torn apart" by them into a food <note>In alchemical theory, "feeding" the stone with gold allows it to reach its final perfection.</note> and coagulates with it into perfection, as I show further in my book, etc.

# The Book is called Trimo-
->sin, in which three powerful Tinctures and other matters besides are found, as follows.<-

---

->Thus writes Salomon Trismosin concerning the Red Life.<-

Many great secrets appear in all things in Nature, which the highest God himself has ordained, so that the children of men wonder at them when such things are revealed to them. The greatest treasures lie in the mountains of the earth, from which men may sustain themselves and get by in this world. For without the earth, man could not live; from it comes food and drink. And were mankind not worthy of these gifts which the merciful God sends us—as everything would surely be used with unthankfulness toward Almighty God—He therefore does not let many treasures be revealed. Thus, much remains hidden in this world because of our unthankfulness. Yet, more is revealed to pious people than they might expect, as I have often read that a poor man has frequently come upon something great in **Gold** <term>☉</term> and **Silver** <term>☽</term>.

Now the **Red Lion** <note>The "Red Lion" is a traditional alchemical term for the final stage of the Philosopher's Stone or the specific chemical agent used to create gold (the Rubedo).</note> is the greatest treasure in this Art and in this world, with which the children of men who possess it can perform great wonders, so that they may attain health and wealth.

Whoever now wishes to work with this must experience great things ordained by the Supreme Queen <note>Likely a reference to the "Queen" or feminine principle in the alchemical marriage (the Albedo stage), or a personification of Wisdom.</note> and the highest spirituality, more than I can write; and he must be a learned artist who understands well the Tinctures and their dissolutions, as well as the governance of the **Fire** <term>Δ</term>, otherwise nothing can be done. For once, this Lion is a clear, joyful tincture that, after augmentation <term>augmentation: the process of increasing the power or quantity of the alchemical medicine</term>, tints many thousands <note>Original: "fl:", likely referring to florins (currency), implying that a small amount of the tincture creates wealth worth thousands of coins.</note>. It transforms the imperfect metals **Lead** <term>♄</term>, **Tin** <term>♃</term>, **Iron** <term>♂</term>, and **Copper** <term>♀</term>—at which I was amazed and awestruck.

**Concerning the Red Lion**

# Now follows the water which is called Mercurial Water, in which gold becomes the Prime Matter, and remains a virgin before and after the dissolution; this is the First Work.

Now take calcined **Gold** <term>Sol</term> and **Silver** <term>Luna</term>, each one **ounce** <term>ounce</term> <note>Original symbol: σ</note>, pound, or lot: taken 8 **drams** <term>drachms</term> dried, 4 pounds or lots. Grind everything small together into a **Salt** <term>Sal</term>; after that take 1 1/2 pounds or lots of **Mercury** <term>Mercurius</term> and of the above-mentioned **Salt** <term>Sal</term> of **Gold** <term>Sol</term> and **Silver** <term>Luna</term> also 1 1/2 pounds or lots. And all this **Salt** <term>Sal</term> should be ground: an understanding laboratory worker should [place] the same upon the **Fire** <term>Ignis</term> until the **Water** <term>Aqua</term> is entirely drawn out. Remove the clay with care, so that the **Salt** <term>Sal</term> does not leak away <note>Original: "in die hosen," a period idiom for leaking or going to waste</note>; for with this **Mercury** <term>Mercurius</term>, we [work] with fresh **Salt** <term>Sal</term> as mentioned above with the same method as before. The laboratory worker should protect himself, for it smells like a Hungarian "Divine Stone" <note>likely a reference to a specific mineral preparation, possibly vitriol-based</note>: it has a rather harsh smell. And when he pours it, he should drink a strong spiced mead-wine.

Take this **Mercury** <term>Mercurius</term>, ground small. Put it into a flask <image-desc>alchemical flask symbol, possibly a cucurbit</image-desc>. Upon this, pour **Spirit of Wine** <term>Spiritus Vini</term>; set it in a **Water Bath** <term>Balneum Mariae</term> and draw it off very gently until it reaches an oily consistency, or when it is half gone, pour the **Spirit of Wine** <term>Spiritus Vini</term> or **Residue** <term>Excrementum</term> <note>Original: Excrementum, referring to the dregs or discarded phlegm of distillation</note> back onto it and draw it off again. Repeat this for a third and fourth time, so that the **Mercury** <term>Mercurius</term> is purified along with the **Residue** <term>Excrementum</term>. If this does not happen, you must pour the **Residue** <term>Excrementum</term> fresh upon the **Mercury** <term>Mercurius</term> and let it **Putrefy** <term>Putrificieren</term>; the **Residue** <term>Excrementum</term> should always stand a finger's height above the matter. When the **Mercury** <term>Mercurius</term> has sat in the **putrefaction** <note>Original: faulag</note> for 6 days, then take the whole matter out of the **Receiver** <term>Recipienten</term>, and **Distill** <term>Distillire</term> the whole substance over the **Alembic Head** <term>Helmb</term>. And bring it over a second time; after that, **rectify** <term>rectificier</term> the distilled **Mercury** <term>Mercurius</term> into the four elements until it has no more **residue** <term>Residenz</term>, so that everything is destroyed and has become a precious burning **Fire** <term>Ignis</term>.

Now take the **Mercury** <term>Mercurius</term> in a Venetian <image-desc>alchemical flask symbol</image-desc>. Place upon it Venetian paper, seven-fold, and an **Alembic Head** <term>Helmb</term> on top of that; set it in clean ashes in very gentle heat: draw it over finely and slowly. And if there is still a **residue** <term>Residenz</term>, draw it over once more through a seven-fold paper in a **Water Bath** <term>Balneum Mariae</term> until the **Mercury** <term>Mercurius</term> has come into the four elements; and this **Mercury** <term>Mercurius</term> is truly **Spiritualized** <term>Spiritualisch</term>, so it should be well preserved.

Naturally, the Earth has now been changed and transformed into

been <note>Continuing from the previous page: "...the soil thrown up in particular places has been..."</note>, the moisture passed down through it from above, from which it became like a mash. ## Entrance of the Universal Tincture. [16].

Regarding its First Essence, which our ancient school calls the **First Matter** <note>original: "Primam Materia"; the fundamental raw substance required for the alchemical Great Work</note>, out of which [the Tincture] is born: it brings with it the most ferocious animals—the **Lion**, the **Crocodile**, and **fiery Dragons**. Thus it will become a **Red Stone**, with which one can perform the <term>Projection</term> <note>the final stage of alchemy where the Stone is cast upon base metals to transform them into gold</note> upon metals.

Finally, three main colors will appear to you in the Tincture: 
First, like a greenish lily <note>original: "gilg"</note> with streaks of <term>Gold</term> and a golden circle. 
Thereafter, the Tincture becomes fixed and indestructible, gray and white, with which one can **tinge** <note>to "tinge" is to transform the color and nature of a metal</note> all liquid metals, using one part for many thousands of parts. 
Thereafter, through red <term>Fire</term>, the Tincture becomes varied red, and then "beyond red," and is a heart above all hearts.

### Universal Tincture of Mr. Hieronymus Crinote

Put it into a vial <term>Mercury (☿)</term> and pour the above-mentioned bright <term>Gold (☉)</term> over it so that it covers it slightly. Place it in a water bath <note>original: "B:M:" for *Balneum Mariae*</note> and the <term>Gold (☉)</term> and <term>Mercury (☿)</term> will entirely become spiritual and volatile. This is called "viscosified" <note>rendered into a thick, oily, or syrupy state</note> and led into the First Matter <note>original: *Primam Materam*</note>. This, resulting from the solution after the first fixation, is the true First Matter. Within this lies the greatest secret <term>Arcanum</term> of the tincture. It is a mistake to call the first dissolution the "First Matter"; that is merely a dissolved spiritual body, which has been made fixed through **Fire (△)**, and yet truly rendered stable <note>original: "figiert worden"</note>.

### Now follows the Final Work, and
->it is precipitated into a stone.<-

**Take [Rx]:** Now the First Matter <note>original: *Primam Materiam*</note> which has been viscosified with the **Mercury (☿)** and **Water (▽)**. Pour the **Mercury (☿)** off gently and dry this mass slowly. Grind it, and the other part which you kept from above, and put it into a flask <note>original: "Urinall"; a pear-shaped glass vessel</note> with a long neck, sealed. Let it be fixed in the heat <note>original: "Eßen," referring to the furnace or hearth</note> using a wick made of seven-fold twine in an oil lamp for 21 days <note>original: "21. ☉, ☽, ♂"; the symbols for Sun, Moon, and Mars represent the first three days of the week, but here signify a duration of 21 days</note>. The work will then proceed. Use a wick of 10 threads and let it stand for 12 days; it will become green and gold-colored. Thereafter, use 12 threads for the wick, and it will become white; the work is then perfectly fixed, stable, and accomplished. Thus, let the work stand in a great, bright **Fire (△)** until it becomes scarlet red. Then the tincture is ready, precipitated, very fluid, and penetrating.

Thus the true Universal [Medicine] is ready and perfect, capable of transmuting <term>Tingieren</term> many thousands of parts when it is re-dissolved. There follows how one should transmute with it; it also heals the greatest heart-sickness <note>in alchemy, "heart-sickness" refers both to physical ailments and spiritual melancholy</note> with great power.

From this tincture, take much or little according to your pleasure. Melt 1000 parts of fine **Gold (☉)** ounce by ounce; no other metal should be present. Project a single part of the tincture upon the **Gold (☉)**; this transforms it into pure tincture. Of this [new] tincture, take 1 part and melt 1000 parts of fine **Silver (☽)**; project it upon them and it will become the best **Gold (☉)**. Do likewise with **Mercury (☿)**, **Copper (♀)**, **Tin (♃)**, **Lead (♄)**, and **Iron (♂)**. Make the metal red-hot like a glowing ingot <note>original: "Zain"</note>; for every 1000 parts, pour 2 parts of the tincture upon it while it glows, and pour it back into the **Fire (△)**; thus it becomes the best **Gold (☉)**, enduring in all tests.

# Universal Tincture of Baron Hieronymus Crinos.

I have seen no tincture described so clearly as this one, in which nothing is lacking; I have also worked it out with God’s help and finished it with great effort. The reason [for the difficulty] was that I did not know the <term>degrees of fire</term> <note>original: "gradus Ignis"; refers to the specific levels of heat required at different stages of the alchemical process</note>, which are otherwise all included in this <term>tincture</term>. For all the <term>philosophers</term> <note>the traditional term for alchemists who sought the "Philosopher's Stone"</note> did not intend it as faithfully as this Crinos did. They kept it strictly hidden from the evil and base world, so that it might not perhaps fall to the share of a godless person. And they considered this well, with a great zeal, for the Highest God does not wish <term>that</term> <note>original: "dz," a common scribal abbreviation for "dass"</note> we should all be rich.

# BOOK OF SUVORETHON

## By Salomon Trismosini.

In this book, the long life of man is found; and a man could well sustain himself for 100 years, if it were not against God's will—for the life of man stands entirely in His divine will and hands. As an example, the great and mighty King in the Kingdom of Xopholad <note>Likely a legendary or mythic figure; alchemical texts often cited Eastern or ancient kings to provide authority to their recipes</note> extended his life to 300 years with the following <term>Arcanum</term> <note>A secret, potent medicinal preparation or "mystery"</note>.

All great lords—indeed, I say both the poor and the rich—whom the Great Lord <note>referring to God</note> enables to prepare for a long life, should treasure this <term>Arcanum</term> above all secrets. They should regard it for the sake of their health, keeping it as hidden as a secret lord keeps himself in private; for within it is the living essence, through which all diseases can be healed and the body is naturally preserved.

Compared to this "Suforethon," all apothecaries must be dismissed with their syrups, which only create <term>Putredinem</term> <note>original: "Putredinem"; Latin for rot or decay</note> and putrefaction in the blood. This <term>Arcanum</term> brings the decayed blood into a renovation of the <term>Humor Radicalis</term> <note>original: "Humor Radicalis"; the "root moisture," a vital fluid in medieval medicine believed to be the fuel of life</note>, making it as pure and fresh as that found in a young child. Furthermore, it is <term>rectificiert</term> <note>rectified or highly purified through distillation</note>, which is a great mystery that God the Lord has placed into this Suforethon for the benefit of mankind.

I, Trismosini, have myself been made new with this secret in the most wonderful and easy way. And if one wished (were it not for the Eternal Wisdom of God), he could sustain himself with this <term>Arcanum</term> until the Day of Judgment. But a pious, God-fearing man seeks after the heavenly goods...

## This is Now the Seventh Tincture
->in order<-
<note>original: "in ordine"</note>

**Y**ou should know that you take strong **Spirit of Wine** <note>original: "Weinweg," likely *Weingeist*; alchemical symbol: ℞</note> as much as 10 lot <note>approx. 150 grams</note> and you dissolve <note>original: "olt," to turn into oil</note> therein 2 Lot of fine **Gold** <note>original symbol: ☉</note>. Then keep the **fire** in great heat; it will become blood-red. Then the Tincture is finished and ready.

Then take 1 part [and] cast it upon 12 parts of molten **Copper** <note>original symbol: ♀</note>; that becomes a tincture. Of that, take 1 part and let 10 parts of fine **Tin** <note>original: "ℤ", often used for *Zinn* (Tin)</note> be in a **crucible** <note>original symbol: □</note>. Cast the part upon it, let it stand for a quarter [hour?] in the **crucible**, then pour it out. This is a high-grade **Gold** <note>original symbol: ☉</note>. Do the same with the **Copper** as well as with the **Tin** <note>original symbol: ♃</note>.

# Salomon Trismosin’s Description of Nine Tinctures.

<note>This section concludes the instructions for the Eighth Tincture, begun on the previous page.</note>
Pour a very strong **Spirit of Wine** <note>original: "Sp: V:", Spiritus Vini</note> upon it, so that it well covers the substance, and begin to distill in a gentle **Water Bath** <note>original: "B: M:", Balneum Mariae</note>. Pour the distilled **Spirit of Wine** back onto it and draw it off again; when this has been driven strongly three times, the vapor of the **Spirit of Wine** rises over the helm <note>the top part of a still</note> so that the sediment stands 2 or 3 fingers high. Then the **Viscosity** <note>thick, oily substance</note> is found at the bottom. Pour the **liquid** <note>original symbol: ∇, representing water or liquid</note> off the top very carefully and make the **Viscosity** dry. Divide this portion into 2 equal parts. Grind <note>original: "Rumbiren," to rub or stir</note> one part for 6 hours in iron, and let it be **fixed** <note>original: "figieren," to make a substance stable under heat</note> until it becomes entirely resistant to **fire** <note>original symbol: Δ</note>. This **Aleph** <note>original symbol: ℵ, often used to denote the "First Matter" or a secret salt</note> is 1 part; apply it to 100 parts of unrefined **Lead** <note>original symbol: ♄</note>. That will become the **Calx Tincture** <note>a powder produced by roasting metal</note>. Of this, take 1 part to 1000 parts of **Lead** in flux <note>molten state</note>; let it sit for half an **hour** <note>original symbol: ⌛</note>, then pour it out. Thus, the best **Copper** <note>original: "C:", likely referring to the metallic body or Copper</note> is produced, stable in all tests, which will precipitate **Gold** <note>original symbol: ☉</note>.

Also, take purified **Copper** <note>original symbol: ♀</note> according to common use, and [add] 100 parts of this aforementioned Tincture. Of this, take 1 part to 1000 parts of fresh **Copper**, let it **mix according to the art** in the **Copper** for just a little while, and pour it out. This produces the highest **Copper** that has ever been made; it is very malleable, and you can proceed thus with all metals: with **Tin** <note>original symbol: ♃</note>, **Lead** <note>original symbol: ♄</note>, and **Iron** <note>original symbol: ♂</note>.

## The Absolon by the short path.

->By Salomon Trismosin<- <note>original: Salomonis Trismosini. Salomon Trismosin was a legendary alchemist, famously described as the teacher of Paracelsus and the author of the "Splendor Solis."</note>

I truly admonish and warn every Christian who wishes to deal with this Art, that he should abstain from all vanity, and above all, from greed and sinful desires. The Absolon is nothing more than the pinnacle of what alchemists achieve; there is no art of <term>tinging</term> metals <note>To "tinge" (German: *tingieren*) means to transform the nature and color of a base metal into gold or silver by applying a small amount of the Tincture.</note> that is as simple and plain in its work. In contrast, other tinctures require much trouble and labor, yet little is found. Among many thousands, hardly one may be found who encounters such a secret, for here the dear God in heaven looks upon the intentions, and whether the heart is qualified for it—those who go to Him in prayer and earnestly persist that He might grant them success in this work, not for themselves alone, but to do good for the poor and the needy, so that they may understand the treasure of great wisdom and have mastery over it. I have held this in my heart and, in the <term>reiteration of the multiplication</term> <note>A process of repeating the final stages of the work to increase the potency or volume of the Alchemical Stone.</note>, I have tinged 1,000 parts with 1 part. I did not have much joy in this, except for passing the time with the poor; whenever I distributed something to them, their thanksgiving to God the Highest was heard by Him.

I have also known ten others who possessed the Art; but God gave them up as evil men. They pursued all manner of evil lusts with it, for their hearts were full of villainy and malice toward their neighbors. Woe to you for your evil conduct and your mouth! You give very good, smooth words and looks, but your heart is full of all manner of wicked cunning. These men exist for the sake of their pride and false tricks.

Then pour the Spirit of Wine back onto it, drawing it off without end; do this eight times <note>original: "8 lang."</note> until the gold becomes volatile. Put it to the test on a glowing coal to see if it is truly volatile; if by its smoke it has become spiritual <note>Converted from a solid metal into a vaporous or "spirituous" state.</note>, then draw the liquid essence from it. Then fix <note>original: "perfigilier." Likely a corruption of "perfici" (to complete) or "figieren" (to fix/solidify).</note> the vessel in gentle heat until it is well coagulated into a stone, yet let nothing rise up. It is important to know that the work should be done in a vessel that can and must keep the spirit alone. Rub this stone with the vessel so as to putrefy it in water; let it stand until the stone turns to water and resolves itself. Put the vessel again in sifted ashes for 30 periods <note>original: "30 ☿". The symbol for Mercury is used here, likely indicating "philosophical days" or cycles.</note> with very gentle heat, until it coagulates into a stone again. This should be put into horse dung <note>original: "fimum equinum." Decomposing manure was used as a natural, steady source of low heat for "digestion."</note> to be resolved until it happens eight times. Perform the coagulation and resolution 15 times, or as long as it takes until it will no longer coagulate, or let it be; thus there remains an indestructible liquid. This is a Tincture prepared perfectly in its essence; therefore, O you, thank God diligently from the bottom of your heart and praise Him.

**Note:** It is to be observed that if it is resolved and coagulated 15 times, the stone will no longer begin to rise <note>Meaning the substance has become "fixed" and stable under heat.</note>.

## Wonders upon wonders have I seen

Among coarse, ignorant artists and laborers in this chemical art, who have sought for Tinctures in common salt <note>original: "$\ominus$"</note>, extracted mercury <note>original: "☿"</note>, and salt <note>original: "$\ominus$"</note> from cattle and human bones, as well as various earths and sulfur <note>original: "$\triangle$"</note> from lead <note>original: "$\hbar$"</note>, zinc <note>original: "Z"</note>, copper <note>original: "♀"</note>, iron <note>original: "♂"</note>, mercury <note>original: "☿"</note>, and whatever the fuming metals may be; nothing sound came of it. Much gold <note>original: "☉"</note> is to be found there, and whoever can separate it through the Art from the antimonial sulfur <note>original: "$\triangle$"</note> has the means to sustain his livelihood. And it is called *Sol obscurum* <note>original: "☉ obscurum"; Latin for "dark sun" or "hidden gold"</note>, because it is made visible <note>original: "visibiliter"</note>; the reason being that the quantity of sulfur <note>original: "$\triangle$"</note> acting within the antimony <note>original: "♁"</note> produces the gold <note>original: "☉"</note>. I say further: if antimony <note>original: "♁"</note> were not mixed with gold <note>original: "☉"</note>, then the mined gold <note>original: "Berg ☉"</note>, when one pours it through [the antimony], would not become so pure and clear, nor so fine. For the exalted gold <note>original: "Elevatische ☉"</note>, alongside the sulfur <note>original: "$\triangle$"</note> of the antimony <note>original: "♁"</note>, tinges the common mined gold <note>original: "Berg ☉"</note> so highly that it lacks nothing in any tests and stands perfect in its power.

And know that the gold <note>original: "☉"</note> in the secret art is the greatest essence in the world, which even those experienced only in common, poor arts...

# The Crowned Tincture of Salomon Trismosin

Trismosin says that if not used correctly, a heavy punishment follows. To those who would be wise in this matter, you must speak of the coagulation in the Earth along with the colors, and especially the color of the Earth called the <term>Raven’s Head <note>original: "Caput Corvi"; the alchemical stage of nigredo, or blackening, symbolizing the death of the old substance</note></term>. This stage often produces such deceptive results that it makes a fool of even an experienced philosopher. Yes, it is said that it turns black. But tell me, dear friend: if you have worked through a tincture, does that first color remain a black-gray earthy color? Or is it seen for a long time as an <term>Antimony <note>original: "🜔"</note></term>-like white? In summary: where there is an error in this color, the entire work is false. This is told to you because one cannot write everything down.

->So now hear and experience it yourself.<-

Take a well-coagulated <term>Gold <note>original: "☉"</note></term> from Hungary. Before starting, let it be refined through the <term>quart <note>a purification process where gold is alloyed with silver and then separated using nitric acid</note></term> and wash it until it is perfectly sweet. Then drop it into rich <term>Antimony <note>original: "🜔"</note></term> and grind it seven times with <term>Spirit <note>original: "🝃"</note></term> or <term>Chibur <note>an alchemical term, often referring to sulfur or a prepared spirit</note></term> upon a smooth <term>Antimony <note>original: "🜔"</note></term> tablet. Let it burn away through grinding and be consumed therein; but let it burn with this vapor using only a small <term>Fire <note>original: "Δ"</note></term>. Do this seven times with fresh <term>Antimony <note>original: "🜔"</note></term> and <term>Spirit <note>original: "🝃"</note></term>. Grind it on a smooth or hard marble stone with a rubbing stone for two full hours. The communication or harmonious agreement, and also the opposition of two natures that are set against each other, which is highly to be praised and wondered at.

## A Dialogue on Alchemy

At this, my worthy friend, tell me—those who wish to be born from a thing should not be displeased; for that which is born shares, for the most part, the same inherent properties as its source, as I will explain hereafter. And thus, neither would a metal come from an egg, nor a crocodile from a metal—though a crocodile can indeed be parched and dried up in the desert. And yet, you have many more reproachful things and sins to set right. To answer your question further and more clearly: metals, in which the heaviness, weight, and elegance are unequal, could not be transformed. But <term>gold</term> <note>symbol: ☉</note> is unequal to other metals, possessing a nobler and more powerful nature. ## A Dialogue on Alchemy

Whoever wished to make **wormwood wine** <note>original: "Wermuth Wein"; wine infused with Artemisia absinthium, valued for its medicinal properties.</note> skillfully might use such an art, by using the herbs in their most delicate **spirit** <note>original: "Spiritu"; the volatile essence or distilled core of a substance.</note> itself. In such a spirit, a power can exist so great that if a small half-measure <note>original: "Maße"; a historical German unit of liquid volume.</note> were poured into a whole measure of wine, it would transform everything into its own nature and properties, including the taste and smell of the wormwood. Oh, what is it that you want from me? # A Dialogue on Alchemy

On the other hand, kings have often used these secrets to their own ruin. Therefore, this art is not to be desired by a wise man unless he is perfect in it, and one who also despises an **overflow of riches** <note>original: "überfließ d' Reichtumben"</note> and could do without all things. And now I hope you understand—as it seems to me—why it happens that the **secrets** <term>Arcana</term> <note>original: "Arcana"; from the Latin 'arcanum,' referring to hidden or specialized knowledge accessible only to initiates.</note> of the art have been known to so few people over so many years.

## Christophilus

But I am of the opinion that these **secrets** were never recorded in any writings or books, but rather, as is also said of the **Kabbalah** <term>Caballia</term> <note>original: "Caballia"; referring to the Jewish mystical tradition of Torah interpretation, which practitioners believed was originally passed down through oral transmission alone.</note>, remained with posterity solely through oral instruction.

## Theophrastus

Although that is consistent with the truth, it is nonetheless hardly believable. In ancient times, this art was recorded in books most clearly, without any **obscuration** <note>original: "Vertunckelung"; literally 'darkening,' referring to the use of allegories and metaphors to hide meaning.</note> or concealment, and was brought from the **Asiatics** to the **European Greeks**.

## Christophilus

XI.

# A Dialogue on Alchemy.

Regarding all various arts, the darkness of the mind can be turned away, as Socrates <note>The Greek philosopher (c. 470–399 BCE), who in this context is cited as an authority on the pursuit of knowledge and the clearing of mental ignorance.</note> himself confesses: namely, that no one is so useless as to have learned an art and kept it to himself, as if he were a poet who does not give sight to the blind, but only turns away the darkness, while the sharpness of sight remains in its present state and history. So it also happens with other arts; and let this also hold true in the perfect knowledge of our **Alchemical Art** <term>Alchimisten Kunst</term> <note>Alchemy is presented here not just as a chemical process, but as a philosophical "art" that requires spiritual clarity.</note>. Let this be the fame of the wise, which is indeed most difficult for those who do not listen to them and only desire riches. But let it be known that riches are the reward of wisdom—riches which are provided with wondrous and manifold delights. And that God, or the dispensation of fortune and His works—no human inventor would recognize this. Meanwhile, the art does not fall behind; and because it is so, the ignorance of men, the lack of wisdom, and the stubbornness of desires—indeed, the "raging steeds of all desires" <note>original: "wüetenden Roß aller Begierden." A reference to Sophocles (c. 496–406 BCE), the Greek tragedian, often used to describe the uncontrollable nature of human passions.</note> as Sophocles calls them—topple justice to the ground. They value this miserable and borrowed life <note>A common Renaissance trope referring to life as a debt owed to nature or God.</note>, along with its damaging usury, far higher than all works of happiness or the best things. And therefore, before they even begin to become wise, the final misfortune befalls them, and the Devil himself, with the most piteous fall and shameful ruin,

->throws them to the ground. Divides<-
->And shatters them<-

## To Create the Air.

Take this aforementioned Earth <gloss>Terram</gloss>, put it into a slanted retort <note>A glass vessel with a long, downward-pointing neck used for distillation.</note> and place it in a sand bath <note>A container filled with sand used to provide even, indirect heat to the glassware.</note>, and distill an oil <gloss>o o</gloss> or spirit above all else; you should continue distilling this until you see that your Black Earth is fixed <gloss>Terra Nigra fix</gloss> <note>In alchemy, a "fixed" substance is one that is stable under heat and will not vaporize.</note>. You should do this until your Earth becomes completely dry, and so it follows <gloss>et sequitur</gloss>. And from this oil, the Air is made by purifying <note>original: *rectificieren*; to refine a liquid through repeated distillation.</note> the oil.

## To Create the Fire.

You should take the fixed Black Earth <gloss>Terram Nigram fixam</gloss> and pour upon it a spirit that was distilled previously. If you wish to have a coagulated Fifth Essence <gloss>quintam Essentiam</gloss> <note>The "Quintessence" was believed to be the purest medicinal core of a substance, stripped of its physical impurities.</note>, or if you wish to have it alone, then pour your distilled oil upon it and let it putrefy <note>A process of slow digestion or fermentation in gentle heat.</note> for 14 days in horse manure <gloss>in Equino</gloss> <note>original: *Equino*; referring to a "horse-manure bath" which provided a steady, gentle heat for alchemical digestion.</note>; so that it may draw out what remains of the Fire <gloss>Δ</gloss> in the Earth. Then distill an oil again; that is entirely Fire <gloss>Δ</gloss>, with the spirit remaining on top. Pour that same liquid back onto the Earth, and set it to putrefy in manure <gloss>in Fimo</gloss> for 14 days as before. Then distill the Fire <gloss>Δ</gloss> out of the Earth; let it "drink" <note>Imbibition: the process of saturating a solid with a liquid until it is fully absorbed.</note> it as before. And place the Air of Heaven on top, and see if the Earth wishes to be fixed <gloss>f: o</gloss> in the Air. Pour the spirit that was distilled before back onto it or over it and distill once more for an oil, which is the Fire <gloss>Δ</gloss>. Keep the Earth and add it to the "dead earth" <note>The *caput mortuum*, or the worthless dregs remaining after all essences have been extracted.</note>. Every time, you should test your Earth in the Air to see if it becomes moist and yet not fixed <gloss>f: o</gloss>. You must pour the distilled Fire <gloss>Δ</gloss> onto it every time, and do this until you see that the Earth remains completely saturated <note>original: *Trincken*; literally "drinking."</note> in the Air; then it is correct.

Item: This is the oil that is distilled for the second time.

## Preparation of the Water.

# An Augmentation with Mercury & Lead. 79

### Process.

Take: 6 Loth <term>Loth</term> <note>A traditional German unit of weight, approximately 15–16 grams or half an ounce.</note> of **Red Lead** <term>Mennig</term> <note>Lead tetroxide, a bright red/orange pigment and oxidative agent.</note> and 4 Loth of **Common Salt** <term>Sal Commune</term>. Grind them both small together and put them into a large **crucible** <note>original: "T", standing for *Tiegel*</note>. Place it in **glowing charcoal** until it becomes incandescent, and stir it constantly with a piece of wood so that it **calcines** <note>reduces to a powder through heat</note> well. Do this in this manner 2 or 3 times. Afterward, **wash away** <term>abluire</term> the salt from it with hot **water** <term>Aqua</term> <note>symbol: 🜔</note>, and you will find the Red Lead as a subtle dust; the subtler it is, the better.

Take of this same Red Lead 6 units <note>original: "6 vngeſt", possibly meaning 6 un-pounded parts or a specific measure</note>: 4 Loth of **Mercury** <term>Mercurius</term> <note>symbol: ☿</note> and 3 Loth of **sublimated** <note>original: "auffgezogen," meaning pulled up through heat</note> **Salmiac** <term>Salmiak</term> <note>symbol: *; Ammonium chloride, used to help metals react</note>, which must have been processed <note>original: "gaillet," likely a corruption of a term meaning purified or refined</note> three times beforehand with **Salt** <term>Sal</term> <note>symbol: Ө</note> and **Iron** <term>Mars</term> <note>symbol: ♂</note>. Take 2 Loth of this mixture. Grind these pieces small and etc. Put them into a glass **flask** <term>Kolben</term>. Over this, pour a strong **Water** <note>likely an acid or solvent</note> so that it covers it fairly well. Draw it off through a **distillation helm** via a **Bain-Marie** <term>B:M:</term> <note>a gentle water bath for heating</note> until it reaches an oily consistency. Pour the **Water** back on and draw it off again to oiliness a second time.

Afterward, pour a good **Spirit of Wine** <term>sp: v:</term> <note>high-proof ethanol</note> over it, in which 1 Loth of **Salmiac** has been dissolved <note>original: "vber na fl:", possibly *übernacht flüssig*, meaning liquid overnight</note> and calcined. Draw the **Spirit of Wine** off from it via the Bain-Marie until nothing more comes over. Pour it back on and draw it off for the third time with the great heat of the water bath, so that the entire substance rises over into the **receiver** <note>the vessel that catches the distillate</note>. This material may also, in part, be **putrefied** <note>allowed to rot or ferment in a gentle heat</note> 3 or 4 times before the final distillation. 

When it is then distilled over and the substance has risen, pour the carried-over material back once more and distill it over again so that everything rises. Then the entire material has entered into the **four elements** and is called the **Hellish Dorras Water** <note>original: *Hölliſch Dorras 🜔*; "Dorras" is an obscure term, perhaps a name or a corruption of a Latin descriptor like *torrens* (torrent/stream)</note>, which turns **Lead** <term>Saturnus</term> <note>symbol: ♄</note> into a viscous substance.

Take: the beaten **Lead**. Put it in a glass flask and pour the aforementioned **Dorras Water** over it so that it is well covered. Set it in a **warm furnace** <note>original: "warms Pfeÿ," likely referring to a heating apparatus or sand bath</note> well-sealed at the top. Let it stand for 4 days, and the **Dorras Water** will consume the **Lead** into a viscous **Mercury** very lovely. Afterward, pour the water off quietly. The Mercury remains behind, and if you wish, you can make a **Living Mercury** <note>liquid quicksilver</note> out of it.

# The Spiritual Sun of Bartholomew Korndorffer. 84.

which <note>referring to a previous vessel or substance</note> [takes] Gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note> and Mercury <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, 10 lots <term>lot: a historical unit of weight, approximately 1/32 of a pound or 15 grams</term>; put a helm <note>the cap of a distillation apparatus</note> upon it and digest it <term>digest: to apply constant, gentle heat over a long period</term> together. Continue this imbibing <term>imbibing: the process of a dry substance absorbing a liquid</term> and digesting for so long until the 10 lots of Gold and Mercury, from the Gold, Mercury, Salts, and Antimony <note>original symbol: ♁</note>, remain at the bottom and through stirring have turned into a green stone. Take <note>original symbol: ℞ (Recipe)</note> a little of this stone for a trial upon a Copper <note>original symbol: ♀</note> plate; if it melts without smoke, it is correct. If not, proceed as before. Put it into a vial in red sand <note>a sand bath used for even heating</note> [with] Mercury 4 <unclear>Gold</unclear>, then it will coagulate into a blood-red Gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note>. It will also require gentle heat <note>original: Linde Essen</note> as the others do, until it becomes fixed <term>fixed: a substance that does not evaporate or change when exposed to high heat</term>. Project 1 lot of this upon 10 lots of Mercury <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, and you will have [Gold] that stands up to every test. **Note:** Before you project the stone upon Gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, it is a medicine to be taken into the human body for all illnesses; administer 4 grains in wine.

# The Spiritual Sun of Bartholomew Korndorffer,

which should be allowed to pass [through the vessel]; rising up like mash and ascending like coals. # The Spiritual Sun of Bartholomew Korndorffer - 85.

# Particular Procedure with the Burning Heaven <note>original: "Brennenden Kürbel"; likely a variant of "Brennenden Himmel" (Burning Heaven) mentioned on the previous page</note>. 87.

A material has deposited itself on the furnace residue <term>Abloß: the dross or slag that settles during the smelting or refining process</term>. Place it in a small crucible <term>Tiechl: a small melting pot</term> to grind it into an oily mass.

Prepare the Antimony oil or Water <note>original symbol: ▽</note> thus: Take the Antimony in a cloth and set a pot; fill it with Aqua Vitae <note>original: A V: V:; concentrated alcohol or "water of life"</note>. Place the Antimony, unbound in the cloth, into the pot in the middle of the Aqua Vitae. Then seal it well with lute <term>Perlutiere: to seal a vessel airtight with a paste made of clay, dung, or glass</term> and cement it <term>Cimentier: to heat a substance in a sealed vessel, typically for a long duration</term> for 12 hours. Grind it small upon Tin <note>original symbol: ♃</note>; put it in a kettle or pan with Water <note>original symbol: ▽</note>. Let it boil a little and filter it. Then, when the Water has boiled away, you will find the Antimony at the bottom of the pan. Moisten this Antimony slightly with common Water <note>original symbol: ▽</note>. Then place it on a cupel <term>Capel: a shallow, porous dish used in cupellation to separate precious metals from lead</term> and let it turn into Antimony or Water. Thus you have the Antimony or Water for moistening, and the Antimony is prepared as it should be.

Carry 14 lots of this Antimony onto well-melted <note>original: m:</note> Tin <note>original symbol: ♃</note>. Let it be well absorbed, then cupel <note>original: Treibt ab; the process of refining by heating in a furnace</note> it. # How One Should Clarify the Seven Metals. 93.

Before you now wish to grant the status of a perfected metal or medium—through this art which you do not understand—to this merely volatile metal <note>original: "Rauch metall," literally "smoke metal," referring to volatile substances like arsenic or mercury that vaporize when heated</note>, and to make the same [perfect] with a perfected metal—such as those you call Gold <term>☉</term> <note>the symbol for the Sun and Gold</note> and Silver <term>☽</term> <note>the symbol for the Moon and Silver</note>, though they can also be imperfect—and to make it good and stable in all tests: this you will accomplish with all the art. You have researched the possibilities of nature within the metals, and in short, you proceed in an orderly way with the impossible, whereby one deceives their own hands, falls into silence, and loses body, honor, and goods.

And only the true art is made and brought to hand by way of a [liquid] drink <note>refers to the "Aurum Potabile" or drinkable gold, a legendary alchemical life-elixir</note>. # Tinctural grading of **Gold** <note>original symbol: ☉</note> with the Black Eagle <note>The "Black Eagle" is an alchemical term usually referring to the sublimation of sal ammoniac (ammonium chloride) or a specific mercurial spirit used to "devour" base metals.</note>.

Moisten it in a glass <note>original: "G"</note> and with the **Antimony** <note>original symbol: ⊕; could also denote Vitriol in some contexts, but Antimony is standard for purifying gold</note> let it cook in a glass until it is reduced to one [measure], then the gold is extracted.

Take: 2 pounds <note>original: lb</note> of this, and 1 pound of **fixed Saltpeter** <note>original symbol: ε fix</note> and filed Alum. Put this prepared material into a cementation pot <note>A "Cement Topf" was used for the process of cementation, where gold is refined by heating it with salts that react with and remove impurities</note> in sand. [Heat it for] 30 hours with a gentle fire <note>original symbol: Δ</note>, then 10 hours even stronger. For the final 10 hours, cover the cementation pot with the sand and build a coal fire <note>original: "Koll Δ"</note> on top of it. Let it cool. From this, take the matter within and reduce it to a <term>Regulus: The metallic mass that settles at the bottom of a crucible after smelting</term>. Cupel this <note>original: "treib ab"</note>, and you will have the yellow grade [of gold]. And it is fixed **Saltpeter**; this is for grading highly. Here end the "Calojan pieces" of Master E. Adler; it is **Lead** <note>original symbol: ℏ</note> that has the elevated **Gold** <note>original symbol: ☉</note> within itself.

This specific procedure <note>original: "Particular stückh"</note> shall be performed by a learning journeyman.

Take 1 1/2 Lot <note>A unit of weight, approximately 1/2 ounce</note> of finely filed **Copper** <note>original symbol: ♀</note>. Grind these pieces well in the open air <note>original: "o: a:"</note>. Pour it upon **Gold** <note>original symbol: $\odot$</note>, and let the vapor <note>original: "stemo"</note> smoke away from it until no more vapor is sensed. Then [add] Realgar <note>original: "Reuschrieße"; arsenic disulfide</note> and **Antimony** <note>original symbol: ♁</note> again: 3 Lot, and reduce these to metal. Let the vapor smoke away from it once more. Do this for a third time, but without reducing it to metal [the third time].

Grind this small, and just like any "parted" <note>Refined or separated</note> **Copper**, add common Sorge <note>A mineral additive, possibly a type of vitriol or salt</note> and **Antimony**, which is also called "ZZ" at this time <note>likely a cipher for zinc or a specific mineral salt</note>. Put these together into a **crucible** <note>original symbol: $\Upsilon$</note> and seal it with luting clay. Place it for 1 1/2 **hours** <note>original symbol: $\square$</note> in hot sand until the **Copper** is cemented away; thus the metals will have ingress <note>The power to penetrate or transform</note> into the **Copper**. <image-desc>A small grid symbol consisting of three vertical and three horizontal lines intersecting like a hash mark.</image-desc>

Take: 1 Lot of **Copper**, federweiß <note>original: "federweiß" - likely fibrous alum or asbestos</note>, and common **Salt** <note>original symbol: $\ominus$</note>, equal parts <note>original: "aa."</note> 1/2 Lot. Let the **Copper** remain entirely within for 1 **hour**. Simmer it <note>original: "Walcheng"</note>, then let it sit by itself in the "sweet purification" <note>original: "süß mundier"</note> until it is ready.

Now take: 1 quintlein <note>Approximately 4 grams</note> of the prepared metal, finely ground in a small paper with a grain of **Borax** <note>original: "Boras"</note>. Let the Lot of **Copper**, which has been prepared, simmer by itself, and throw [the paper] upon it. Let it go for 1/4 **hour** in the open air. Afterward, cupel it with **Lead** <note>original symbol: $\hbar$</note>; thus you have fixed **Copper** <note>Copper that has been chemically "stabilized" so it does not oxidize, a step toward turning it into gold</note>.

Thus far I have taught my friend. I tell you, if the purified **Copper** <note>original: "♀ Purgatum"</note> appears halfway with the "yellow needle" <note>A testing tool used to assay the quality of gold</note>, take 1 Lot of **Gold** <note>original symbol: $\odot$</note> and add the same **Copper** to it. Let it melt. Add 1 quintlein of the three prepared metals to it. Let it sit for 1/4 **hour**. Add another quintlein [of the metal]; thus everything remains as the best **Gold**. Only take care that the vapor on the test-shard <note>original: "scherben" - a cupelling dish or ceramic fragment</note> flows strongly with the metal, so that the "ZZ" can afterward take hold of the metal.

# An Ancient Process

With fresh <term>materia</term> <note>the raw material or "first matter" of the alchemical work</note>, take 1/2 part of this <term>Mercury</term> ($\mercury$), and pour 1/2 part of <term>aqua fortis</term> <note>original: "scheidewasser"; literally "parting water," typically nitric acid used to separate gold and silver</note> over it. After it has been distilled over 5 or 6 times, it should be sealed in a glass <note>original: "Zusammengeschlagen," likely referring to hermetically sealing or luting the glass vessel</note> and closed up immediately so that the <term>spirits</term> <note>the volatile gaseous components of the substance</note> cannot escape. Then place all of this in a <term>Mary’s Bath</term> <note>Latin: "Balneum Mariae"; a warm water bath used for gentle, consistent heating</note> and let it undergo <term>putrefaction</term> <note>the process of breaking down or "rotting" the matter to release its essence</note> for 12 or 6 days with a gentle <term>fire</term> ($\triangle$). 

Then draw off the <term>phlegm</term> <note>the watery, inactive distillate</note> from it. Afterward, take it out and place it in a sand <term>cupel</term> <note>a sand bath used for higher temperatures than a water bath</note> and attach a <term>luting</term> or a small receiver to it. Give it a gentle <term>fire</term> ($\triangle$) to roast the <term>Water</term> ($\nabla$) <note>here referring to the liquid contents or the solvent</note>, and keep it constantly sealed. Observe when the spirits begin to move; then the spirit, along with the <term>Mercury</term> ($\mercury$), will rise white and hot and quite clearly. Keep the <term>Water</term> ($\nabla$) <note>the vessel/seal</note> tight so that no spirit escapes, for this is a pure spirit.

Now take the remaining <term>Mercury</term> ($\mercury$) or <term>Copper</term> ($\text{\venus}$), grind it very small, and add very sharp <term>aqua fortis</term> to it. Place it once again in the <term>Mary’s Bath</term> for 20 days. Then draw off the spirit as before until it reaches an oily consistency. Then seal it up again and distill the spirits further in the sand bath, and pour that <term>Water</term> ($\nabla$) <note>the distillate</note> together with the other <term>Mercury</term> <term>Water</term> ($\nabla$). 

Then, once more, grind the remaining residue of <term>Mercury</term> ($\mercury$) and <term>calcine</term> <note>to reduce a substance to powder through heat</note> it. Extract its <term>Gold</term> ($\odot$) <note>the essential "solar" essence of the metal</note> from it. Take the <term>Gold</term> ($\odot$) that you have extracted and put it into the <term>oil of Mercury</term> so that it dissolves. Then you will have a fine <term>Gold of Jupiter</term> ($\odot$ $\text{\jupiter}$) <note>likely a reference to a purified state of tin or a specific stage of the "Great Work"</note>; this is a <term>ferment</term>. 

You should pour out the <term>Gold of Jupiter</term> ($\odot$ $\text{\jupiter}$) very well. From its spirit—if you wash it with the <term>Water</term> ($\nabla$)—it will soon dissolve and become as red as blood. Then place this solution back into the <term>Mary’s Bath</term> to <term>putrefy</term> for approximately 8 or 9 days. After that, draw off its <term>phlegm</term> in the <term>Mary’s Bath</term> until only the oil remains. 

Finally, place it under a <term>blind helm</term> <note>a still-head without a spout, used for refluxing</note> and set it in a sand bath or in ashes so that it <term>coagulates</term> <note>thickens or solidifies</note> into a stone. Then you have the highest gift of God. That same stone <term>tinges</term> <note>transforms the nature and color of a metal</note> 10 lbs of lead, or 6 lbs in casting, into <term>Mercury</term> <term>Gold</term> ($\mercury$ $\odot$).

# An Ancient Process described by
a Franciscan Monk, abandoned 109 years ago
and found again.

Take: 2 pounds of <term>vitriol</term> <note>a metal sulfate, likely iron or copper</note> and <term>alum</term> <note>a potassium aluminum sulfate used as a mordant and astringent</note> solution; into this, add 1 pound of <term>antimony</term> (<term>$\antimony$</term>) [or] warm water. Grind the <term>part</term> <note>original: "t," likely "Teil"</note> well with <term>gold</term> (<term>$\odot$</term>) in a mortar, then add the <term>salt</term> (<term>$\text{S}$</term>). Once that is done, let it dry slowly; thus the <term>vitriol</term> is prepared. Take 12 pieces of <term>honey</term> (<term>H</term>) and rub them <term>thoroughly</term> so they are completely mixed. Place this on a warm <term>gold</term> (<term>$\odot$</term>) plate that has been made very smooth, like a spoon. In this way, the <term>honey</term> (<term>H</term>) all turns into a <term>water</term> (<term>$\nabla$</term>), and the <term>vitriol</term> remains lying on the plate. Pour the <term>spirit-water</term> (<term>$\nabla$</term> <term>$\text{S}$</term>) into a retort where the neck is somewhat wide. Distill it back and forth, discarding the clean residue. This distillation should be performed 3 times. Once you have the <term>spirit-water</term> (<term>$\nabla$</term> <term>$\text{S}$</term>) in the <term>vitriol</term>, proceed as is further described hereafter.

## A Genuine Process:

Distill using the <term>alembic</term> <note>a chemical still consisting of two vessels connected by a tube</note> three, two, or four times until it has no more residue; in this way, you may obtain the water (<note>Water/Aqua</note>) more plentifully and usefully, if you wish to have it. But then the <term>spirits</term> <note>volatile essences</note> of gold (<note>Gold/Sol</note>) and silver (<note>Silver/Luna</note>), according to their use, are driven into it with their scent, just as you did before.

Likewise, if you want to <term>graduate</term> <note>to refine or increase the purity and color of a metal</note> half a <term>lot</term> <note>a historical weight, approximately 15 grams</note> of <term>elixir</term>, then take (<note>Recipe/Take</note>) 12 <term>lots</term> of <term>calamine</term> <note>zinc ore, often used to turn copper into brass or to color gold</note> with which the water of graduation has been made. Pour this over it, but ensure the elixir has been previously granulated or beaten thin. Distill it <note>original: "Eßen," likely referring to the distillation process</note> quite gently down to an oiliness <note>original: "olitet," referring to the consistency of a thick oil</note>, then pour spirit <note>symbol for water/spirit: ▽</note> onto it. ## FIRST TREATISE,
<note>original Latin: "TRACTATUS PRIMUS."</note>

This philosopher's stone is brought forth through the way of grounding Nature; of this the holy philosopher speaks, saying: this Stone proceeds from a growing and greening thing. For why it is green and brings itself forth, or is brought upon Nature, is because through this a thing becomes better, more perfect, and greening at its appointed time. It is also that which one [takes] on the way and secret of the <term>Art</term><note>In alchemy, "Art" refers to the specific skills and laboratory processes used by the alchemist to assist or accelerate natural processes.</note>, to <term>separate</term><note>original: "Schey" (Scheiden). The process of separating the pure from the impure.</note> and to <term>rot</term><note>original: "faule" (faulen). Refers to "putrefaction," a key early stage in the alchemical process where the matter must "die" to be reborn.</note>, so that one produces help for Nature through Art. [Nature] rusts and rots by itself, until time gives it the right form; and Art is nothing but a tool and preparer of the <term>Matter</term><note>original: "Materien." The physical substance being transformed.</note>, as well as the appropriate form, and that which is the effect [brought forth] with practiced wisdom. 

For just as little as Art is able to make a new beginning, etc., if the first beginning of things cannot be given, so it is also not necessary that one separates and grasps Art from the natural processes and grips of the minerals, as they have their first beginning in the earth. Art has another way than Nature, and therefore it also has other and more distinct tools. And thereafter, Art also gives birth from the previously sent natural roots—just like the beginning of Nature—to final things which Nature through itself could nevermore bring forth; for Nature is able to give birth to nothing on its own. The things through which the metals might be born imperfect by Nature could [be made perfect] only [by] the secrets...

<summary>This page introduces the first treatise of the manuscript, defining the relationship between "Art" (alchemy) and "Nature." It argues that while alchemy cannot create life from nothing, it acts as a tool to help Nature complete the perfection of minerals and metals.</summary>

<header>Splendor Solis</header>

...is of natural virtue, and thereby such a filling occurs into the moist things. But the <term>philosophers</term><note>original: "philosophi." In this context, the "philosophers" are the ancient and medieval alchemists who sought the secrets of nature.</note> do not speak of this filling; for them, their filling is a strengthening or an <term>imbibition</term><note>original: "ein trinckung," literally "a drinking." In alchemy, this is the process of adding liquid to a dry substance until it is saturated.</note>, whereby the saturated things reach their fiery state, so that they may turn green and grow. 

In this filling, the moisture is united with the <term>saturation</term><note>original: "trunckenheit," literally "drunkenness." Alchemists used this term to describe a state where a substance has absorbed as much liquid as it possibly can.</note> and is not destroyed, so that the moisture holds the saturation together; and this is properly a <term>grinding</term><note>original: "Zerreibung." Also known as trituration, the physical reduction of matter into fine powder.</note>. However, if the moisture is entirely separated from the saturation, then the ability to separate the saturated parts and transform them with honor is lost. 

The philosophers do not want this <term>incarnation</term><note>original: "incarnation," meaning the process of taking on a bodily or solid form.</note> either; rather, they want their filling, their imbibition, grinding, and <term>calcination</term><note>original: "Calcionierung." The process of heating a substance to high temperatures to purify it or reduce it to a powder.</note> to occur in such a way that the natural moisture and saturation are united with each other and freed from superfluous moisture. 

This is just as when heat enters the common belly and is consumed, and from it the nourishing power and moisture are drawn—by which Nature is sustained and fed, and its superfluous parts are separated. Yet, every thing must be prepared according to the properties of its nature, as 

->should be fully noted here<-
->in the aforementioned<-
-><term>Philosopher's Stone</term><note>original: "Stein der Weisen." The ultimate goal of alchemy, a substance capable of turning base metals into gold and granting eternal life.</note>.<-

# SECOND TREATISE

Morienus <note>original: "Morisines." Likely referring to Morienus Romanus, a legendary 7th-century alchemist.</note> speaks: you should know that the entire work of this art is divided into and concluded by two tasks. These are linked together so that when one is performed, the other begins and completes it; thus the entire mastery is perfected. However, these tasks do not occur except within their own specific material. To understand this properly, one must first know that Nature creates every birth and fruit in a <term>Mercury</term> [☿] <note>original: "☿," the symbol for Mercurius.</note> arising from the potential of the metals out of <term>Sulphur</term> [🜍] <note>original: "🜍," the symbol for Sulphur.</note> and <term>Earth</term> [♁] <note>original: "♁," likely referring to Earth or Antimony in this context.</note>.

And Ferrarius <note>Likely referring to the 13th-century alchemist Ferrarius or Efferarius, author of "De Alchimia."</note> asserts this in the "Questions on Alchemy" in the 25th Chapter: that Nature generates our metals from the very beginning of nature. She takes no earthy substance or <term>Water</term> [🜄] <note>original: "🜄," the symbol for Water.</note> mixed with very white, agile, and forward Earth; rather, she dissolves this into a steam or vapor and raises it up into the veins or crevices of the earth. This right steam or vapor, which joins together, is precious in its moisture and fiery nature, thus united with one another until a substance is formed which one calls <term>Mercury</term> [☿]. And this is now the beginning and the very <term>First Matter</term> <note>original: "Erste Materia." The primary, raw substance from which all metals are naturally formed.</note> of the metals, as was also mentioned above.

Therefore he speaks again in the 26th Chapter, where he says: those who wish to follow Nature should not take Mercury [☿] alone, nor Mercury [☿] and Sulphur [🜍] joined together from common materials. Instead, they should take that which Nature herself has joined together, well-prepared and cooked in a noble fluidity. In such a Mercury [☿], Nature began with her first operation and ended in a metallic nature, and there she ceased. For she has accomplished her part and left everything else to the Art <note>The "Art" refers to the alchemist's work—completing what Nature began.</note> to finish into a perfected <term>Stone of the Philosophers</term>. The philosophers say that one should begin where Nature has left off, and should take the <term>Sulphur</term> [$\triangle$] <note>original: "$\triangle$," the symbol for Sulphur or the element of Fire.</note> and the <term>Mercury</term> [$\mercury$] <note>original: "$\mercury$," the symbol for Quicksilver/Mercurius.</note> which Nature has joined together in the very purest form at home; for in this has occurred the skillful union which no one else can demonstrate in the Art in such a way. And Nature has done all this for the sake of the birth of the metallic form. However, this same material, which is thus informed by Nature, benefits the Art for the sake of unfolding the power that is then found residing within the material.

And thereafter, some alchemists also calcine the <term>Gold</term> [$\odot$] <note>original: "$\odot$," the symbol for Gold or the Sun.</note> so that they may bring it to dissolution and the separation of the elements, until they bring it into a spiritual, subtle nature and purity—the <term>Mercury</term> [$\mercury$] and <term>Sulphur</term> [$\triangle$] natures. And this is then the very closest material, which compares most closely with the <term>Gold</term> [$\odot$], to receive the form of the hidden Stone of the philosophers. And this is what Aris <note>original: "Arles." Likely referring to Pseudo-Aristotle, who was frequently cited in medieval alchemical texts, particularly in fictional dialogues with Alexander the Great.</note> means in the speech to King Alexander, regarding that which has the name <term>Gold</term> [$\odot$] for our Stone, and with which kings are adorned and crowned. Although this <term>Mercury</term> [$\mercury$] alone is the material and a single thing, yet the thing is so manifold in its action and in its name that no one can boast of understanding it easily. And this is done, as Rosinus <note>A Latinized name for Zosimos of Panopolis, a prominent early alchemist.</note> says, so that not everyone might be able to attain it. It is likewise a work, an action, and a vessel, all of which is manifold by way of comparison to all things that are contained within Nature. For thus speak the philosophers: Dissolve that which is now <term>Earth</term> [$\earth$] <note>original: "$\earth$," the symbol for Earth or Antimony.</note>, and then distill and coagulate it; make it ascend and descend, pour in [liquid] from above... <note>original: "Trunckh ob ein," likely referring to the process of imbibition, where liquid is added to the dry matter.</note>

# THIRD TREATISE <note>original: "TRACTATVS TERTIVS"</note>

Hermes, a father of the philosophers <note>Referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the mythical founder of alchemy to whom many foundational texts were attributed.</note>, says: after the end of this world, heaven and earth are to come to our aid. No one can, through heaven and earth alone, [attain] the two aforementioned operations <note>original: "geschickligheiten"; these are the specific manual and spiritual skills required for the work, mentioned on the previous page.</note>, but it sounds far too much in wisdom before they are brought to an end and understood through the comparison of figures, as follows hereafter.

And this is the first parable: God first created the Earth quite plain, white, and very fertile, without spirit and sand, stones, mountains, and valleys. Through the influence of the planets and the working of Nature, the Earth has now been transformed into many forms: on the outside, into hard stones, high mountains, and deep valleys; on the inside, into strange colors and things, namely the ores and their beginnings. And with such things, the Earth has completely lost its original form, and it happened that on some sides it became raised, or the Earth was heaped up thick, large, long, white, and brownish.

Yet, through the constant working of the sun's heat, a sulfurous, misty, and smoky breath <note>The alchemist here describes the "exhalation theory" of metal formation, where vapors (Sulfur and Mercury) are cooked by the sun inside the earth to create minerals.</note> was created within, which permeated the entire Earth down to the abyss, and produced in the cold and moisture of the Earth a watery mist, also foggy and airy, all of which were enclosed within the Earth.
