# Splendor Solis.

## The Third Parable.

Hermes, the first master of this art, speaks thus: that the <term>▽: Water</term> of the air is between heaven and earth. It is that in which things live, for through its moisture and warmth it is the medium between opposites, such as <term>△: Fire</term> and <term>▽: Water</term>. And that same <term>▽: Water</term> has rained down upon the earth, by which the earth has become sweet, like honey. And it happens that this blood <note>A common alchemical term for the life-force or "sap" of the work</note> brings forth many kinds of colors and fruit; and in their midst has grown a great tree with a silver trunk, which spreads out to the corners of the world. Upon its branches sat many kinds of little birds; they have all flown away toward the <term>☉: Sun or Gold</term>, and the Raven’s Head <note>The "Raven's Head" or *Caput Corvi* signifies the Nigredo (blackness) stage, which here transitions into Albedo (whiteness)</note> has become white. 

The same tree brings many kinds of fruit: the first are the finest pearls, and it is called by the philosophers <term>Terra foliata: Leafy Earth</term>; the third is the finest <term>☉: Sun or Gold</term>. This tree also gives the fruit of health: it makes warm that which is cold, and the warm it makes cold; the dry it makes moist, and the moist it makes dry; it makes the hard soft, and the soft hard. This is the end of the entire art.

Regarding this, Pictor <note>Likely referring to an alchemical authority or "The Painter"</note> speaks in the third word: "The <term>♃: Jupiter or Tin</term> together with the Stone are precious words of the entire mastery." Galen <note>Galen of Pergamon, the famous Greek physician</note> also means this when he speaks of the *Lunatica* or *Bera* <note>Likely referring to Moonwort (*Botrychium lunaria*), a plant traditionally believed to have alchemical properties due to its moon-shaped leaves</note>; it is a root that is a metallic earth, having a red stem, covered or illuminated with silver in its essence. It decreases according to the course [of the moon], and also produces or receives flowers according to that course. After three days, if one puts it into <term>♃: Jupiter or Tin</term>, it changes into a perfect <term>☽: Moon or Silver</term>. And if one "drinks" <note>possibly meaning "absorbs" or "washes" in a chemical sense</note> it further, it converts into <term>☉: Sun or Gold</term>. That same <term>☉: Gold</term> converts a hundred parts into the purest <term>☉: Gold</term>. 

Virgil mentions this tree in the sixth book of the *Aeneid*, speaking in a fable: how Aeneas went to a tree, and when he plucked a branch, another grew in its place. <note>This refers to the "Golden Bough," which Aeneas required to enter the underworld.</note>

## Sixth Figure

->### The Third Parable###<-

Hermes, the first master of this art, speaks thus: that the <term>Water (▽)</term> <note>original: "Wasser"</note> of the air is between heaven and earth. It is that in which all things live, for through its moisture and warmth it is the medium between opposites, such as <term>Fire (△)</term> and <term>Water (▽)</term>. And that same <term>Water (▽)</term> has rained down upon the earth, by which the earth has become sweet, like honey. And it happens that this blood <note>In alchemy, "blood" often refers to the vital "mercurial" sap or the life-force within the material</note> brings forth many kinds of colors and fruit; and in their midst has grown a great tree with a silver trunk, which spreads out to the corners of the world. 

Upon its branches sat many kinds of little birds; they have all flown away toward the <term>Sun or Gold (☉)</term> <note>original: "Sonne oder Gold"</note>, and the Raven’s Head <note>The "Raven's Head" or *Caput Corvi* is the traditional symbol for the *Nigredo*, the initial stage of decomposition and blackness</note> has become white. 

The same tree brings many kinds of fruit: the first are the finest pearls, and it is called by the philosophers <term>Leafy Earth</term> <note>original: "Terra foliata"</note>; the third is the finest <term>Gold (☉)</term>. This tree also gives the fruit of health: it makes warm that which is cold, and the warm it makes cold; the dry it makes moist, and the moist it makes dry; it makes the hard soft, and the soft hard. This is the end of the entire art.

Regarding this, Pictor <note>Likely referring to the alchemical authority *Senior Zadith*, whose name was sometimes corrupted to "Pictor" or "The Painter" in various manuscripts</note> speaks: "That the earth of this tree is the Leafy Earth, and its fruit is the food of life."

<summary>This page presents the Third Parable, using the "Philosophical Tree" to illustrate the stabilization of volatile elements and the transition from the black Nigredo stage to the white Albedo stage. It describes the alchemical "Water of the Air" as a mediating force that harmonizes elemental opposites to produce the "fruit of health."</summary>

# The Third Parable.

Avicenna speaks in the chapter on **moisture**: when heat acts within a moist body, it first produces a **blackness**. This occurs because cold has triumphed; a mist raised by the heat covered and gathered the entire earth. This same earth became putrid and stinking in the darkness. Afterward, the turbulence of the sea and the water-floods subsided. But as the fullness of the earth sank away through heat, the King of the Earth appeared; he rejoiced with a delightful voice and said through his redemption: "Who is living bodily with me, and reigns in my clarity from my Royal Throne?"

And while darkness surrounded all things, they saw a bright **Morning Star** rise over the King at daybreak. The light of day illuminated the darkness; the clear Sun, shining through the clouds, brought forth many colors and forms with its stars and brilliance. A musk-scented fragrance rose up from the earth. The Sun shone with clear radiance and, in its perfection, enlightened and renewed the King of all glory. 

He was fully adorned, and even Heat himself marveled at his supreme beauty. The **Sun** and **Moon** were decorated with three precious crowns: one made of **G.** <note>likely Gold</note>, the second of **S.** <note>likely Silver</note>, and the third of **O.** <note>possibly Orichalcum or a reference to the third alchemical principle</note>. In his right hand, he saw a body containing **seven stars** which all gave a glittering shine, and in his left hand was a scepter, upon which sat a **white dove**. This dove demonstrates the nature of its silver and its silver wings.

Regarding this, Aristotle says: "The destruction of one thing is the birth of another." <note>original: "corruptio unius est generatio alterius"</note> This is spoken in reference to the **Masterful Art** <note>Alchemy</note> and its cycle of destruction, being renewed through its **essential moisture**, which is its perfect life.

# Splendor Solis
## The Fourth Parable.

Menaldus the philosopher <note>original: "Menaldus philosophus"; likely a reference to a figure in the "Turba Philosophorum," an influential early alchemical text</note> speaks thus: I command all my descendants that they make the **bodies** spiritual through **dissolution**, and prepare the **spiritual things** corporally through a **gentle cooking**. Concerning this, Senior <note>Senior Zadith, an alias for the 10th-century Arabian alchemist Ibn Umail</note> speaks thus: the spirit dissolves the bodies, and in this dissolution, it draws out the **soul**, and the soul is transformed into the **spirit**, and the spirit shall be joined again to the body; then it remains permanent with the body, and prepares the body spiritually in the power of the spirit. The philosophers give this to be understood when they speak in such a figure: a human or earthly form, a **Moor** <note>In alchemy, the "Moor" or "Ethiopian" represents the stage of *Nigredo*, the initial blackening and purification of the matter</note>, stands in clay, or black, unclean, foul-smelling slime. To his aid comes a young woman, beautiful of face, even more beautiful of body, and most highly adorned with clothes that were of many different colors. But she was adorned with **white wings** on her back; the feathers were like the most beautiful white peacocks, and had golden quills, and the quills were adorned with shining pearls. She has a crown on her head of pure <term>Gold (represented by the symbol ☉)</term>, and upon the crown a silver star. About her neck she has a necklace of fine <term>Gold (☉)</term> in which is set the most noble Ruby that no King is able to pay for. She has on her feet <term>golden (☉)</term> shoes, and from her there went out the most noble scent, exceeding all spices <note>original: "Aromata"</note>. She clothes this man with a **purple garment**, and leads him with her toward heaven. Of this Senior speaks thus: it is a living thing that dies no more, for it is established with an **eternal increase**.

# Splendor Solis

## The Fifth Parable

The philosophers assign two **bodies** to this Art, namely **Sun** and **Moon** <note>In alchemical symbolism, the Sun and Moon represent the primary duality: gold and silver, or the active (Sulfur) and passive (Mercury) principles</note>, which are the Earth and the Water. They also call them **Man** and **Woman**. And there are born "4" children: "2" males, which are **heat** and **cold**, and "2" females, which are **moisture** and **dryness**. These are the **four elements**, and they create the **fifth essence** <note>Original: "fünffte wesen"; the Quintessence, a celestial substance beyond the four physical elements</note>, which is the **white Magnesia** <term>Magnesia: In alchemy, this refers not to the modern element magnesium, but to the "primal matter" or the refined substance of the Philosopher's Stone</term>, which is not false. Senior <note>Senior Zadith, a name used for the 10th-century Arabian alchemist Ibn Umail</note> concludes this by saying: when these five are assembled, they shall be one single thing, from which the **Natural Stone** is made. Avicenna <note>A Latinized name for the Persian polymath Ibn Sina (c. 980–1037), whose works were central to medieval alchemy</note> says: if we are able to reach the fifth, then the end of our purpose has arrived.

To illustrate such a parable, the philosophers describe an **egg**, for within it are four joined things. The first, the outermost, is the **shell**, which is the **Earth**. The **white** is the **Water**. But the **membrane** between the water and the shell is the **Air**, and it separates the Earth from the Water. The **yolk** is the **Fire**, and it has a subtle little skin around it, which is the more subtle Air; it is closer to the fire and separates the fire from the water. In the very center of the yolk is the **fifth**, from which the young chick forms and grows. Thus, in an egg are all the powers along with the matter from which a perfect nature is created. And let this now also be so in the
->**Noble Art**<-

# Splendor Solis
## Figure 9

->The Comparison<-

...**yolk** is the **Fire**, and the tiny **point** within the yolk—from which the chick grows—is the **fifth essence** <note>original: "fünffte wesenheit"; also known as the Quintessence. Alchemists believed that just as a chick emerges from a tiny speck in the egg, the Philosopher's Stone emerges from a hidden spark within raw matter</note>. 

Thus, we see in the **egg** a perfect likeness of the whole Art. For just as the egg is composed of four distinct parts—the shell, the membrane, the white, and the yolk—so too is our work composed of the **four elements** <note>Earth, Water, Air, and Fire</note>, which are joined together by a fifth principle.

Furthermore, the philosophers compare this work to a **Human Being**, for man is also composed of the four elements. His **bones** are Earth; his **blood** is Water; his **breath** is Air; and his **natural heat** is Fire. But the **Soul**, which is the life given to him, is the **fifth essence**.

For this reason, the figure is depicted here as a **Hermaphrodite** <note>In alchemy, the "Rebis" (from the Latin "res bina," meaning "double matter"). This two-headed figure represents the successful union of the Solar/masculine and Lunar/feminine principles</note>. It has two heads, representing the **Sun** and the **Moon**, joined in a single body to show that the Work has reached a state of perfect balance. 

The figure holds the **egg** in its left hand, signifying that the entire secret of the universe and the Stone is contained within this simple, natural form. In the right hand, it carries a **shield** or mirror marked with concentric circles, representing the stages of purification and the layers of reality that the alchemist must peel back to reach the dark, hidden center of matter. The **wings**—one white like the moon and one red like the sun—show that the transformed matter has gained the power to "fly," or to transcend its base, heavy nature and become a spiritual substance.

<summary>This page concludes the analogy of the egg, comparing its structure to the four elements and the "Fifth Essence." It introduces the Hermaphrodite (Rebis) as a symbol of the perfect union of opposites necessary to complete the alchemical Great Work.</summary>

# Splendor Solis

## The Sixth Parable

**Zosimus** <note>Zosimus of Panopolis, a Greco-Egyptian alchemist from the late 3rd/early 4th century, whose mystical visions are foundational to alchemical literature</note> says that he wishes to show, through a vision he had, a **Man** who was **Dead**, and yet his body was white to the highest degree, like **Salt**. His limbs were divided, and his head was of **fine gold**, but severed from the body. Beside him stood a misshapen man, cruel and black of face, who held a **two-edged sword** in his right hand, stained with blood. He was the slayer of the good man. In his left hand, he held a note <note>Original: "Zettl"; a slip of paper or scroll</note>, upon which was written:

> » I have killed you so that you may receive an **abundant life**; but I will hide your head so that the world shall not see you. And your body shall rot in the earth, and I will bury it so that it may decay, and multiply, and bring forth **innumerable fruit**. «

<image-desc>An alchemical illustration framed in black, depicting a glass flask (cucurbit) with a golden crown on its neck. ### The Third Article

**The** third [operation] is Sublimation, through which the previously mentioned moisture of the earth is digested <note>In alchemy, "digestion" refers to the application of gentle, consistent heat over a long period, similar to how a body processes food.</note>. For when the matter is reduced to earth, it passes into the fluidity of the air, and the earth alone rises up as pure, airy clouds, like an egg <note>This refers to the "Philosophical Egg," the sealed glass vessel where the transformation takes place. The rising vapors represent the spirit separating from the dross.</note>. This is the spirit—washed, whole, and purified. It is the Tincture, the <term>ferment</term> <note>original Latin: "fermentum"</note>, the <term>animated</term> <note>original Latin: "animatum," meaning the matter has been "given life" or "ensouled"</note> spirit. It is the purest matter of the Stone which then arises through Sublimation; it is the density produced from its own vapor, granted by God through the moderation of all things. And thus, its own nature and property remain.

This is the true philosophical Sublimation, through which the **Perfect Whiteness** <note>The "Albedo" or white stage of the Great Work. This follows the "Nigredo" (blackness) and signifies that the matter has been thoroughly cleansed of impurities.</note> is accomplished. For this reason, this Art is compared to **women's work** <note>A common alchemical metaphor. # On the Governance of Fire △ <note>The triangle symbol △ represents the element of Fire.</note>

What follows concerns the Governance of Fire: if a thing is deprived of heat, no stability or permanence will remain. The order of nature transforms into the Sun, which is to say—as has been much discussed—that the spiritual is made physical, and they are brought home together. Regarding these two planets <note>The Sun and Moon, representing the male/sulfuric and female/mercurial principles.</note>, <term>Senior</term> <note>Likely Senior Zadith (Zadith ben Hamuel), a 10th-century philosopher frequently quoted in alchemical texts.</note> speaks thus: "I am a hot and dry Sun, and you, Moon ☾, are cold and moist; and when we are joined together in marriage, I shall pour into you a burning light." That is to say, through the teaching and mastery of the ancients, the renewal of moisture shall be received, and Sun and Moon will become transparent. In the <term>Ladder of Philosophers</term> <note>original Latin: *Scala phisicorum*. A reference to the *Scala Philosophorum*, an alchemical treatise describing the steps to the Stone.</note> it is written thus regarding Fire: the heat or the fire of the entire Work is in a linear form. For some say that the heat of the first stage should be like the heat of a brooding hen; others say like the natural heat of the digestion of food and the nourishment of the body; others say like the heat of the Sun when it is in <term>Aries</term> <note>original: *Wid* (Widder). The first sign of the zodiac, representing the gentle warmth of early spring.</note>. Remarkably, the Stone is also brought to completion without [excessive] action; nevertheless, the skill consists in maintaining a gentle and moderate heat, which shall last until the matter has solidified and has changed into the White [stage]. And it is compared to the Sun's heat when it is in Aries and begins to shine in <term>Taurus</term> <note>original: *Stier*. The second sign of the zodiac.</note>; once the Whiteness appears, the heat must be increased until the complete drying out or hardening of the Stone. And the heat then becomes like the Sun's heat when it is in Taurus and also entering <term>Gemini</term> <note>original: *Zwilling*.</note>. And when the Stone is now dried and hardened, the fire is strengthened again until it is perfectly Red and is released from the fire clothed in royal garments. And this heat is compared to the Sun's heat when it is in <term>Leo</term> <note>original: *Löben*. The Lion, the house of the Sun, representing the peak of summer heat.</note>, which is its highest dignity. Therefore I say: enough has now been spoken concerning this explanation or governance of the fire.

# On the Colors that Are Produced During the Whitening of the Stone

## Regarding the process of making it white

Miraldus the philosopher speaks in the <term>Turba</term> <note>original: *Turba Philosophorum* (The Assembly of the Philosophers), one of the oldest and most influential Latin alchemical texts.</note>: it blackens twice, it yellows twice, and it becomes Red twice. One obtains many different colors, and the color changes according to how the heat is directed. No matter how noble all these colors appear, the most important ones—regarded as the primary colors—are these: namely Black, White, and Red. Between these, all sorts of colors appear, especially after the White and the first Redness. Miraldus reports this, though not because it is an incomplete color, as <term>Ciliator</term> <note>Pietro d'Abano (c. 1250–1316), a famous physician and philosopher known as "The Conciliator."</note> says. It barely remains in the <term>Materia</term> <note>The physical substance being worked upon in the vessel.</note> long enough for one to see it; however, the yellowish color that appears after the perfect White and before the Redness shows itself for a time in the matter, which is why the philosophers have also considered it a primary color. Miraldus speaks as noted above, though it is not produced for as long as the Black and the Red, which remain in the matter for a significant duration. The Black and the Red occur twice, but the perfect Black appears in the most gentle heat. Regarding this, <term>Senior</term> <note>Senior Zadith (Zadith ben Hamuel), a 10th-century alchemist.</note> and Ciliator speak thus: the <term>roasting</term> <note>original: *Rösching*. Refers to the calcination or drying of the substance.</note> has occurred in the gentle warmth until the blackness passes away from it. And for that reason, <term>Luas</term> <note>Lucas, another philosopher cited in the *Turba Philosophorum*.</note> the philosopher says in the *Turba*: guard yourselves against strong Fire <note>original: Δ, the alchemical symbol for Fire.</note>, for behold, if one applies an excess of Fire in the beginning, it will become Red before its time, and that is of no use. For in the beginning of its governance, you should have the Black, thereafter the White, and at the last, the Red.

Daldus the philosopher says in the *Turba*: Cook your composition until you see it is white, and cook it in the <term>vinegar</term> <note>In alchemy, "vinegar" often refers to a transformative acid or solvent rather than common household vinegar.</note>; to separate the Black from the White is a sign, and it approaches <term>fixation</term> <note>The process of making a volatile substance stable so that it no longer evaporates or changes when exposed to heat.</note>.

# Splendor Solis.

## Destructive Heat, and the Metallic Moisture from it, and the Tincturing Power.

Then is also accomplished the philosophical <term>putrefaction</term> <note>The stage of decomposition or "blackness" where the material breaks down to be reborn; the text uses the word *füllung*, likely a variant of *Fäulung* (rotting).</note> or ripening, of which mention was made at the beginning of this booklet; and the same is made manifest, as was said before, and the hidden is brought forth. Of this <term>Senior</term> <note>Zadith ben Hamuel, a 10th-century Arabian alchemist often cited in Western texts.</note> says: the ripening is the first [stage] and bears witness to the greatest secret; it is also the true separation of the elements: that which is moist, it makes dry, and that which is dry, it makes [moist] and renders it softer. When everything has been turned to ash, then it is usefully prepared, and this is the "grinding" of the philosophers. Therefore Senior says: let the <term>calcination</term> <note>The process of reducing a metal to a powder or "ash" through intense heat.</note> be useful, so that from it [something] may come.

It is also the <term>decoction</term> <note>A process of "cooking" or boiling a substance to extract its essence.</note> of which all the philosophers speak, finally <term>Albertus Magnus</term> <note>A 13th-century Dominican friar and polymath credited with many alchemical discoveries.</note> speaking thus: in all the arts, there is none that follows Nature so closely as <term>Alchemy</term>, and this is because of the cooking and forming; for it is cooked in fiery and watery metallic <term>Water</term> <note>symbol: ∇</note> which possesses most of the Sun and a little of the matter. It is also the philosophers' <term>affation</term> <note>A term for "roasting" or exposing the substance to dry heat.</note> or roasting, for the self-sufficiency is consumed in a gentle <term>Fire</term> <note>symbol: △</note>. And above all, one must beware that the spirit is separated from the body and dried from the body, or it will not be opposed to the body and will not be perfect.

It is also the philosophers' distillation or clarification, which is nothing other than a cleaning of things and a vanishing of the moisture, and it is made firm with <term>coagulation</term> <note>The process of changing from a liquid to a solid state.</note>. The philosophers speak of the whole work, of which <term>Hermes</term> <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure regarded as the founder of alchemy.</note> bears witness: his power is the Sun, his power is whole; if it returns to a constant and useful effect, as follows hereafter, where one may become [successful]. For it is nothing other than the desire for all natural things to be accomplished; for Art, which follows in truth and not in likeness, as other arts follow, the eloquent Senior speaks thus: he does not praise one who can accomplish this Art without Nature, indeed daily with such nature as has been instilled in Nature from heaven above.

And one boils within it, making <term>Mars</term> <note>symbol: ♂</note> out of dead <term>Saturn</term> <note>symbol: ♄</note>, or making a white <term>Tincture</term> <note>A medicinal or transformative essence</note> from the <term>Crocus of Mars</term> <note>original: "Crocum ♂"; usually refers to a reddish iron oxide powder</note> of white <term>Saturn</term> <note>symbol: ♄</note>. In this way, you have begun the Wisdom, even though the philosopher says: nothing is closer to the <term>Sun</term> <note>symbol: ☉</note> than <term>Saturn</term> <note>symbol: ♄</note>, for the reward is within him. And all secrets are drawn toward him; however, this is not spoken of the common <term>Saturn</term> <note>The author distinguishes between common lead and the "Philosophical Lead" used in the Art.</note>.

Likewise, the Marcasite of Bayerdege <note>likely a reference to a specific mineral source or region, possibly "Beiradege"</note>, which is the glow of the darkness of the Earth. A coagulated little spark, as Morienes <note>Morienus Romanus, a legendary hermit-alchemist</note> says, is also compared to <term>Copper</term> <note>original: "As"</note>, <term>Orpiment</term> <note>original: "Auripigmento"; a deep orange-yellow arsenic sulfide mineral</note>, and <term>Tutia</term> <note>Zinc oxide collected from furnace flues</note>.

Likewise, many things that are not mineral at all are used, from the four <term>Complexions</term> <note>The four humors: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile</note>, to the <term>Basilisk's</term> <note>A mythical serpent-king</note> blood. And many such superfluous things and mineral things, such as solar Alum, <term>Copper</term> <note>original: "As"</note>, and others, for the sake of their many different properties.

But above all things, Alphidius <note>An Arab alchemist frequently cited in medieval texts</note> warns us and says: "Dear son, guard yourself against the spirits, bodies, and stones that are dead, as recounted above, for in them there is no Way; neither will you find your purpose or intent, for their power does not increase but rather comes to nothing." Regarding this, Senior says: "First it became like an egg, thereafter a <term>Sun</term> <note>symbol: ☉</note>, and through manifold labor it became at last a <term>Mercury</term> <note>symbol: ☿</note> of the philosophers..."

# Mirror of Alchemy

## Preface

In many and various ways, the philosophers <note>The "philosophers" here refers to the ancient alchemists, often called "natural philosophers."</note> of old spoke with one another. Through their writings, as if in darkness and with a voice shrouded in mist, they have left us obscured. This is an art above all other arts, the most noble; and yet they left it as if under a cloud of doubt. They did not do this without cause, for they did not wish for their writings to be shared with or benefit their own children or strangers to whom the truth was not deserved. For they previously spoke of such things orally with one another, and also concealed and hid such things in the secrecy of faith. And everything that they encountered further in their parables <note>original: "Paraboln"; refers to the allegorical stories and symbols used to hide chemical processes.</note>, they understood through those same parables. They required no open speech toward one another, nor toward their other good friends, and no one was more certain of this than they.

Secondly, they did not want the gift of God and the secret of the art to be made public and revealed. They ensured that the wicked <note>original: "Boßhafftigen"; referring to those who would use alchemy for greed or selfish ends.</note> should never come to it—only those who possess the art, to whom God clearly reveals it and worthily gives it. For the art would be given in vain or uselessly to the unwise and senseless people. Therefore, to those who desire and are worthy to grasp this art, to them we wish to give and write the whole perfect art, in true truth <note>original: "Wahrheid"</note>, naked and unhidden, and without hindrance.

<gloss>Mirror of Alchemy, philosophers, parables, the wicked, truth</gloss>

<summary>This preface explains the historical reason for alchemical secrecy, arguing that ancient masters used cryptic parables to keep the "noble art" from the unworthy. The author promises to break this tradition by describing the art plainly for worthy readers.</summary>

# Mirror of Alchemy

And the noble discourse, which leads by a shorter path and brings one to an infinite joy.

And therefore I wish to write this, and divide it into seven chapters—neither too few nor in too much excess, but only what is necessary and useful to know. I will describe seven manifest chapters for you, in which you will finally find the mastery of our opinion and undertaking. Therein, understanding is always maintained with subtlety; a clear and subtle teaching is always found among the philosophers <note>The "philosophers" are the historical alchemists.</note>, while among the laity <note>original: "Laÿen"; refers to the uninitiated or those without specialized knowledge.</note> one finds difficulty and coarseness. In these seven chapters, if you view them diligently and run through them with steady, industrious study, you will find within them the whole understanding of the Art, and the opinion of the philosophers upon which you may study and ground yourself. Think upon it powerfully and steadily for a long time until, by God's grace, you have extracted the meaning and the work according to your entire will.

I have promised to write the Art without any deficiency, and also without any trickery—completely and openly, without any doubt—for those who have previously worked a little in <term>sublimating</term> <note>original: "sublimieren"; the process of heating a solid to turn it into vapor and then back to solid to purify it.</note>, <term>descending</term> <note>original: "Descendren"; distillation by downward heat.</note>, <term>distilling</term>, <term>fixing</term> <note>original: "Figieren"; making a volatile substance "fixed" or resistant to fire.</note>, <term>calcining</term> <note>original: "Calcionieren"; reducing a metal to a powder through dry heat.</note>, <term>dissolving</term> <note>original: "Soluieren".</note>, <term>coagulating</term>, and <term>incorporating</term>, and in other uneven things and infinite deceits. Although these things are named and written everywhere in all the books of the philosophers and also in other deceitful books, I say finally to those same people who work in the retreating and deceptive arts—such as in the four <term>spirits</term> <note>original: "Spiritibus"; in alchemy, these are usually mercury, sulfur, arsenic, and sal ammoniac.</note> of alchemy, and in the seven <term>metals</term>, and also in <term>alums</term> <note>original: "Aluminibus"; mineral salts.</note>, <term>borax</term>, and

# Mirror of Alchemy.

## The First Chapter.

### The Description of the Art and Expla-
### nation of Alchemy: What it Actually is in Itself.

In many and more ancient books and writings of the philosophers, there is found quite openly the description and explanation of this same art; therefore, we must also take note in this first chapter of this same meaning and explanation. Concerning this, <term>Hermes</term> <note>original: "Hermes d' philosophus"; referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure regarded as the founder of alchemy.</note> the philosopher writes to us and says thus: <term>Alchemy</term> <note>original: "Alchimia."</note> is an art of the metallic, or of metal, made from one and through one, simply put together. And joined from the union of the most noble things, which overcome one another through knowledge and efficacy, it will—by that same natural mixture—transform the species of metals, converting them into something better.

Another philosopher writes thus: Alchemy is an art that teaches how to transform every species of metal, one into another; and this must happen through a specific <term>medicine</term> <note>original: "Medicinam od' Artzney."</note> or remedy, which is then manifest and described in many books of the philosophers. And concerning this, it should be known that alchemy is such an art that is named after a philosopher who was called <term>Alchimus</term> <note>A common, though likely apocryphal, medieval etymology attributing the name of the art to a specific person.</note>. And the art teaches how to make a medicine—that is, a remedy—which is called an <term>Elixir</term>, such that when it is cast upon the imperfect metals, it makes them perfect and good; that is the reason for its invention.

# The Second Chapter.

## Of the Origin of Metals.

In the words just described, I have completed and finished the first chapter. And now in the second, I will fully explain the origin of minerals, or the ores of the mines: how and from what they naturally best spring forth and are created. And concerning this, it is first to be noted that the origin of minerals, ores, or mining products is nothing other than <term>Mercury</term> [☿] and <term>Sulfur</term> [🜍] <note>The "Sulfur-Mercury theory" was the standard medieval explanation for the composition of metals; sulfur provided the "spirit" or combustible quality, while mercury provided the "body" or metallic luster.</note>. From these two things all metals are created and born.

Therefore there are many and diverse forms, and they are distinct from one another; but nature always intended to make <term>Gold</term> [☉]. However, the adverse and manifold <term>accidents</term> <note>original: "Zufäll"; in Aristotelian philosophy, these are external factors—like impurities or improper heat—that interfere with a natural process.</note> that occur produce various adverse metals in the disruption, as is quite clearly described and found in many books of the philosophers. According to whether the two aforementioned, Sulfur [🜍] and Mercury [☿], are pure or impure, the metals are created or born accordingly: such as Gold [☉] and Silver [☽], Copper [♀], Lead [♄], Tin [♃], and Iron [♂].

# The Seventh Chapter

## Concerning Projection or Tincturing

Now, concerning the preparation of the perfect and masterful work and labor, to bring to a complete and total end the great and excellent <term>Elixier</term> <note>Elixir: In alchemy, this is the "Philosopher's Stone" in liquid or powdered form, capable of transmuting base metals or healing the body.</note> White and Red, one must know how the proportion—that is, the <term>Außwerffung</term> <note>Original: "Außwerffung." Translated here as Projection: the final stage of the Great Work where a tiny amount of the Stone is "thrown" onto a molten base metal to transform it.</note> or <term>Tingierung</term> <note>Tincturing: the process of imbuing a substance with a new quality or color; here, the transmutation of metal.</note>—is to occur. This is the final labor in this work, for which we have waited a long time with eager joy; concerning this, we wish to provide teaching and instruction.

Now, to speak of the White <term>Elixier</term>: the White <term>Elixier</term> <term>Tingiert</term> without end, and whichever metal is imperfect, it brings to a state of perfect metal, which is to say, a great, stable, and true metal. However, it is important to know that one metal is "heavier" <note>In this context, "heavier" implies a metal that possesses more of the required qualities or "spirit" to reach perfection.</note> or possesses more toward perfection than another. And although the <term>Elixier</term> <term>Tingiert</term> every metal and makes it perfect, it nevertheless <term>Tingiert</term> much more easily and effectively those metals that are closer to perfection than those that are further from it. And since we now find one metal that is closer to perfection than another, we will spare you the effort and address you thus: that we do not need to name those which are further from perfection and those which are closer.

If you now diligently read through my chapters and consider them well, you will find therein—entirely revealed and uncovered—which metal is closer or further from perfection than the other. This is beyond all doubt and requires only a subtle understanding, provided you take good note of my aforementioned words.

### Mirror of Alchemy "144"

Take 1 part of the **Tincture** and mix it with 1,000 parts of metals that are closest to perfection <note>In alchemy, "perfection" refers to gold and silver; the author suggests using metals like refined silver as a base for the final transformation because they are already "near" the goal.</note>, and put it all together into a vessel that is suitable for it, and seal it very well, and place it in a melting furnace according to the philosophical opinion. And at first, give it gentle **Fire** <note>original: "Δ", the alchemical symbol for the element of fire.</note>, and afterwards strengthen the fire and proceed step by step until they have lovingly united with one another, and let this happen over the course of three days.

Thereupon, however, one shall take 1 part of that [mixture] and cast it upon 1,000 parts [of metal]; and this shall also be done and considered with the metal that is closest or most similar to perfection rather than another. For there is always a greater and more neighborly unity, friendship, and love between the **Elixir** or **Tincture** and the nearest perfect metal than with those metals that are further from perfection. Therefore, the nearest metals are always to be chosen. And let that be your labor—a work of one day, or one hour, or even a single moment—which is then divine. Therefore, may the Almighty God be praised forever and eternally, amen.

# Key to Chemical Manual Procedures

->.1.<-

## The Philosophers' Royal Water.

Recipe: Gold <note>original: ☉; the Sun</note> that has been calcined <note>reduced to powder by heat</note> to a yellow color, and Silver <note>original: ☽; the Moon</note>, 2 pounds each of calcined Salt <note>original: 🜔</note>. Distill 1 pound of this according to the usual practice, and drive the spirits out thoroughly. Weigh this recipe and set everything aside except for 1 Lot <note>a historical weight, approximately 1/2 ounce or 16 grams</note>. Let 1 pound be made from it; thus you have the Recipe of the Philosophers.

->.2.<-

## Essentified Mercury

Recipe: Gold <note>original: ☉</note> and Silver <note>original: ☽</note>, an equal amount of each. Mix them together and let them lie gently in an earthenware vessel until the moisture is consumed. Grind the mass into a fine powder. In a bowl or vessel, make a hole in the bottom. Place 1 pound of Quick Mercury <note>original: ☿ V. V., likely hydrargyrum vivum</note> into 1 Lot, and drip it on in portions. Then put it back, place the Lead <note>original: ♄</note> upon it, and continue the process until everything comes together. Put this mixture into a coated flask <note>an "armored" or "luted" glass flask reinforced with clay/sand to withstand high heat</note> that is sufficiently tall, with an alembic head luted <note>sealed with airtight paste</note> upon it. Distill <term>♒</term> <note>original symbol: ♒ (Aquarius), used here to denote distillation</note> the mercury out as is the custom. Then throw away the dregs <note>original: "feces"</note> and distill <term>♒</term> the mercury by itself, without any additions, two more times, or as often as needed until it rises alone and leaves no more dregs behind it.

Recipe: Then take the Philosophers' Recipe, and in it place 1 pound of this distilled <term>♒</term> mercury into a flask. Let it stand, then draw it off. Repeat this recipe often; drive the mercury upwards until it rises as white as snow. Throw away the dregs that remain at the bottom <note>original: "in fundo"</note> and are black. Pour the recipe again over the dregs—that is, over the mercury—and distill it, and distill <term>♒</term> again as before. Do this as long as no more dregs

### ->* 3 *<-

## The Frozen Ice-Water.

Recipe: Take 1 pound each of Essentified Mercury <note>original: ☿ Essensificati</note> and Crude Antimony <note>original: ♁ Crudi</note>. Pound the Antimony very small, then rub the Essentified Mercury well into it. Immediately place this into a coated flask <note>a "luted" glass flask reinforced with a layer of clay to protect it from direct heat</note> that is neither too tall nor too wide. Place a "helm" <note>an alembic or still-head</note> upon it that has very short pipes, and a side-flask for a receiver. Join everything together well and lute it <note>seal the joints with an airtight paste</note> so that nothing can escape.

Then, place it in a sand-bath <note>original: Sand Capellen; a container of sand used to distribute heat evenly</note>. At first, apply heat gently; you will hear the Mercury <note>original: ☿</note> reacting with the Antimony <note>original: ♁</note> with a sizzling and crackling sound. First, a "phlegm" <note>a watery distillate</note> like an oil will come over, then the "frozen ice-water" will pass over, appearing just like icicles <note>this likely refers to the crystallization of antimony trichloride, known as "Butter of Antimony," which solidifies at room temperature</note>.

Keep the Antimony and the "icicles" together carefully; this is the Frozen Ice-Water from which springs the Water of the Philosophers' Mercury <note>original: Aqua ☿ philosophorum</note> and the Mercury of Life <note>original: ☿ Vite; Latin: Mercurius Vitae</note>, which you may use as you wish.

### ->* 4 *<-

## The Philosophers' Mercurial Water.

Recipe: Take the Frozen Ice-Water along with its oiliness in whatever amount you wish. Distill it by itself <note>original: per se</note>, without any additions, two more times into a vial. Thus you have the Philosophers' Mercurial Water <note>original: Aquam Mercurialem philosophorum</note>.

Now one must take care: if the ice-water reacts very strongly and is too exposed in this final coagulation, some of the subtle spirits may escape. To prevent this, one should add the phlegm <note>the watery distillate collected earlier</note> that came over previously—in 3 or 4 parts—back to the dissolved ice-water and coagulate it again with it, for the subtle spirits must remain therein. ### Augmentation of the Mercury of Life <note>original: Augmentatio ☿ Vitæ</note>.

**Take:** of the prepared Mercury of Life <note>A white powder derived from antimony, used in Paracelsian medicine</note>, approximately one part, in a coated flask <note>a "beschlagen Kolben" is a glass vessel reinforced with a layer of clay and hair to withstand high heat</note>. Let it be consumed or devoured within, then let the flask cool slowly, so that it will be coagulated. Then break the flask and place the coagulated mass <note>original: Coagulum</note> upon the marble to fix <note>original: f:; likely abbreviation for *fixatio*, the process of making a volatile substance stable under heat</note>. In this way, the fixed Mercury of Life holds the spirits <note>volatile vapors</note> of the unfixed Ice Antimony so that they do not flow away from it. Fix and coagulate this according to the rules of the art <note>original: m : : a :; abbreviation for *manu artis* or *modo artis*</note> for the fourth time, as the process requires. Then you will have a much better Mercury of Life than when it was first made, for it consumes the spirits from the first work, which must thereafter remain with it. From this work, you may take half the portion, or as much as you wish, and use it, and continue to augment the remainder.

# The Practical Procedure for Instruction

Place small phials or flasks into the ash or into the <term>B: M:</term> <gloss>original: Balneum Mariae, a water bath named for Mary the Prophetess, used for gentle, even heating</gloss>. Seal them well and let them "fix" <note>To "fix" or "fixate" a substance in alchemy means to make a volatile substance solid or stable under heat.</note> in gentle warmth until they reach dryness. When the matter is calcined and coagulated, take it out of the glass and grind it upon a stone. Put it back into a flask and let it sit for 8 or 9 [days] in the ash or the water bath, and in another furnace, let it "reverberate" <note>Reverberation involves heating a substance through reflected heat from the roof of a furnace, rather than direct flame.</note> in the ash.

Afterward, take the <term>Qu: Es:</term> <gloss>original: Quinta Essentia or Fifth Essence, the purest medicinal or spiritual part of a substance</gloss>. You must extract the <term>Qu: Es:</term> 3 or 4 times in this manner, so that the white gold <note>original: "Weiße $\odot$"; likely referring to the purified metallic residue once the "soul" or color has been extracted.</note> or the fine white gold is purely separated. You must unite all of this <term>Qu: Es:</term> with your previously distilled gold and proceed with the <term>Stone</term> <gloss>original: Lapide, referring to the Philosopher's Stone</gloss>, which you will find in the First Process under number 9.

On this page, all corrosive nature is stripped from the <term>Qu: Es:</term> by the <term>Spirit of Wine</term>. If you wish to use it for internal consumption <note>original: "Verzerung," referring to medicinal ingestion.</note>, distill a distilled brandy <note>original: "Brennw." or Branntwein.</note> away from it several times, so that the corrosive nature is entirely removed. With this <term>Qu: Es:</term>, gout <gloss>original: Podagra</gloss>, leprosy <gloss>original: ausatz</gloss>, and quartan fever <note>A fever (often associated with malaria) where symptoms recur every four days.</note> can be driven away, and a person may be preserved in health until their appointed hour. If you wish to increase the heat, you may use sand instead of ash; then nothing will easily go wrong. However, you must pay close attention to the color, just as I instructed you regarding the previously described <term>Stone</term> <gloss>original: Lapide</gloss>. Thus, at this Number 6, you find the correct instruction for the <term>Qu: Es:</term>.

# A Tincture or Elixir
### — By an Unknown Philosopher.

Also, note the beginning of these two tinctures, for white and for red. The **water** <term>symbol: $\nabla$</term> of **mercury** <term>symbol: ☿</term>, you shall first make it thus: Take 1 pound <note>original: lli; Libra</note> of **Tin** <term>symbol: ♃</term> and melt it in a **crucible** <term>original: T; Tiegel</term>. And when it is melted, put into it **quicksilver** <note>original: ☿ V: v: p; likely "mercurius vivus," or living mercury</note>; it becomes an **amalgam** <term>an alloy of mercury and another metal</term> from this. Clean it truly until no more threads come from it, and let the **amalgam** become quite dry. Then take that same **amalgam** and take an equal amount of the finest crystalline **vitriol** <term>symbol: ⊕; a sulfate mineral</term>, and rub them very well together on a clean grinding stone so that they are well combined and mixed. Thereafter, lay it on a **glass** <term>original: G</term> plate, not too thick, and set it in a warm cellar that is damp; thus it will turn into a **water** <term>symbol: $\nabla$; referring to deliquescence, where a substance absorbs moisture from the air to become liquid</term> and flow down into a glass vessel.

This is the **water** <term>symbol: $\nabla$</term>. And what remains on the stone or **glass** <term>original: G</term> plate, that is the **Tin** <term>symbol: ♃</term> with the **Mercury** <term>symbol: ☿</term>, and some **Mercury** <term>symbol: ☿</term> flows into the **water** <term>symbol: $\nabla$</term>. So see that the **water** <term>symbol: $\nabla$</term> is beautifully separated from it, and keep it with diligence. And the dregs <note>original: feces</note> that remained lying on the **glass** <term>original: G</term> plate are no longer good for this **water** <term>symbol: $\nabla$</term>; throw those all away. And likewise, cooking **mercury** <term>symbol: ☿</term> in this **water** <term>symbol: $\nabla$</term> is very effective; keep that also wherever you wish, but no fire is needed for this **water** <term>symbol: $\nabla$</term>.

Furthermore, it should be noted that you must **purify** <term>original: Purificieren</term> the first **water** <term>symbol: $\nabla$</term>. To do so, put the **water** <term>symbol: $\nabla$</term> into a **glass flask** <term>original: Kolben G</term> and set it in a warm **digestion bath** <note>original: Roßwerckh Und haber; literally "horse-work and oats," referring to the steady, gentle heat produced by fermenting horse manure</note>, inside it, as if in a chapel or small vessel, and let it stand in an uneven warmth for one month. Thereafter, distill it once at a boil in a **Mary's Bath** <term>original: B: M:; Balneum Mariae, a water bath</term> through an **alembic** <term>a distillation cap or head</term> into a **glass receiver** <term>original: G</term> so that the opening is well **sealed with lute** <term>original: perlutiert; sealed with alchemical putty or clay</term> and bound with good dough-strips <note>original: fladen; likely a flour-based paste used for airtight sealing</note>, so that the noble **water** <term>symbol: $\nabla$</term> cannot evaporate away.

->Instructions for the manual techniques.<-

Concerning the **Tincture of the Sages**, and how, after the tinting <note>the process of transmuting a base metal into a precious one</note>, it shall also be refined in the fire <term>$\triangle$</term> upon the cupel <term>test</term> <note>original: *auf dem Test*; a shallow, porous vessel used in assaying or refining precious metals</note>.

The natural masters say that this tincture is **black** in the beginning, **white** in the middle, and after it has been processed with a strong fire <term>$\triangle$</term>, it becomes **red** or the color of gold <term>$\odot$</term>.

Another philosopher speaks thus: The heat in the furnace or pan causes a ripening in the ore. As the heat works within the **tincture**, it first makes it white, and thereafter with a greater fire <term>$\triangle$</term> it becomes yellow. After that, if the fire <term>$\triangle$</term> is strengthened even more, it turns a beautiful red. This stage, the color of gold <term>$\odot$</term>, is called *Bralinum* <note>a term for the deep red stage of the alchemical process</note>, the red corals. The burning sulfur <term>$\triangle$</term> <note>original: alchemical symbol for sulfur (triangle over a cross)</note> is called **Red of Sulfur** <note>original: *Rubrum sulphuris*</note>, the red pigment is called **Red Orpiment** <note>original: *Rubrum Auripigmentum*</note>. And if the matter remains white, it is called **Lead of Copper** <note>original: *Plumbum Eris*</note>, a "lead of the resin," and **Virgin of the Metals** <note>original: *Virgo Metallorum*</note>, the delicate or pure plate <term>lamina</term> of lead. In this way, the philosophers have given names to this Tincture or Elixir.

Furthermore, one should know of this praiseworthy **Medicine of the Human Heart**, used to drive away all bodily illnesses with this high and mighty tincture.

Furthermore, there are many fools who think they can make **Potable Gold** <note>original: *Aurum potabile*; a legendary liquid medicine believed to grant longevity</note> from common gold <term>$\odot$</term> alone. They claim it is the best medicine to heal all diseases. There are also some physicians, being quite greedy, who claim it is the best for healing all illnesses. However, this is all against nature, and such a substance is not true **Potable Gold**. They also say it is very good to give to the sick, and that one should show the gold <term>$\odot$</term> to the patient, for looking at gold <term>$\odot$term> serves the sick person well. But that it actually creates health—that is not true. Rather, the true **Potable Gold** comes from the power of the most perfect Elixir; it is a medicine that drives away all remaining illnesses of the body.

# All Sorts of Specifics

It has been the opinion of all philosophers and masters of nature, and also of those who understood it, concerning common gold <term>$\odot$</term> <note>the alchemical symbol for gold and the sun</note> alone. His theory is: our creation is based solely on nature—that is, from the elixir of our tincture.

## Arnoldus speaks.

Thus, it also possesses a powerful virtue against illnesses and afflictions, surpassing all other medicines. For it gladdens the human spirit and drives away old age; it does not allow the blood to rot nor the phlegm <term>phlegmam</term> <note>one of the four bodily humors, traditionally associated with water, coldness, and sluggishness</note> to dominate. ## procedure <note>original: "processus"</note>

# For a Tincture upon the Mercury of the Sun and Moon <note>original: "Pro Tinctura auff den Mercurium Solis et Lunae"; in alchemy, the Sun (Sol) represents Gold and the Moon (Luna) represents Silver.</note>

Take 4 lb of <term>Saltpeter</term> <note>symbol: 🜔; also known as nitre or potassium nitrate</note>. Put it in a pear-shaped pot where it resolves by <term>Fire</term> <note>symbol: 🜂</note> into <term>Water</term> <note>symbol: 🜄</note>. Into that same water, put 12 lb of well-purified <term>Saltpeter</term>. And stir it well as [usual]. Thereafter, take 3 lb of <term>Mercury</term> <note>symbol: ☿; quicksilver</note> with <term>Gold</term> <note>symbol: ☉</note> and <term>Silver</term> <note>symbol: ☽</note> that has been purified 8 or 10 times. Press the mercury through a cloth <note>original: "Bar hat," likely referring to Barchent or a fine cloth sieve</note> into the water. Stir it well so that the mercury disappears and becomes pure. Strain it likewise, let it settle, and then place a stone upon it. Grind it small, put it into a <term>Sublimation vessel</term> <note>original: "Sublimatorium"; a vessel used to heat a substance until it turns to vapor and then solidifies again at the top</note> and sublimate it. In doing so, start with a gentle fire for 41 [periods] <note>symbol: □; likely hours or days</note>. Afterward, make it a little stronger, so the smoke rises and becomes as white as snow. Let it cool by itself (beware of the dust, for it has become **Poison** <note>original: "Gifft"</note>). Wipe off the mercury and grind it small.

Take 3 ounces or 3 lb of this mercury to 1 lb of <term>Silver</term> or <term>Gold</term> that has been very finely divided. Grind it as [usual] and put it into a <term>Glass vessel</term> <note>symbol: 🜖; a matrass or round-bottomed flask</note>. Set it in the chamber in ashes within a furnace. Maintain a gentle fire beneath it for 8 or 9 [weeks] long, and attach another flask that is <term>well-sealed</term> <note>original: "Perlutiert"; sealed with a "lute" or airtight clay paste</note>. Give it fire. When the mercury has [consumed] the silver, it will rise up with it, and a portion will pass into the receiving flask. Let it cool, break it open, and grind that which has risen together with that which remained at the bottom. Put it back into a glass vessel with a receiving flask before it, well-sealed. Leave it for another 8 or 9 weeks in gentle warmth. Thereafter, give it a strong fire, so that even more silver rises. Perform this work often and for a long time, until the silver rises with the mercury and nothing remains at the bottom.

In the same way, proceed in another glass vessel and furnace with the fine <term>Gold</term>. Do this also so that it rises and ascends. Afterward, take each separately. Grind it small and pour hot <term>Vinegar</term> <note>symbol: †; likely Acetum or vinegar used for cleaning amalgams</note> over it. Then rub it well by hand, and it will thus become **living mercury**, as beautiful and as capable as any man has ever seen.

# Procedure.

From the **sal ammoniac** <term>✳︎</term>, **vitriol** <term>▽</term>, **nitre** <term>⊕</term>, and **alum** <term>⊡</term>: you must first pour them together into a glass to rot <note>original: "Putrificieren"; the chemical breakdown of matter by gentle heat, often associated with the first stage of the Great Work.</note> in a **water bath** <term>Balneum Mariae</term> for 8, 9, or 10 days. Afterwards, filter it purely, for the rotting process will produce dregs <note>original: "feces"; the solid impurities or sediment left after the chemical reaction.</note>. And when this has been done, pour the three aforementioned pieces <note>The resulting filtered liquids.</note> together and place the mixture in the **water bath** to rot; however, it is better if it is rotted in a flat **heat** <term>original symbol: Δ</term>, namely in **philosophers' dung** <note>original: "fimo Philosophorum"; a slow, gentle, and constant heat produced by decomposing manure, or a chemical furnace designed to mimic that steady warmth.</note>. In such rotting, let it remain for 40 **days** <note>original symbol: "d o".</note>. The longer it stays, the more it is "corrupted" <note>This refers to the transformation of the substance as it breaks down to be reborn.</note>. It also tends to be full of small crystals in the spirit; but even so, do not take it out before 40 **days** have passed. Then, transform it into a **mercury** <term>☿</term> in which the entire mastery of this art is completed, for in it we have everything that we desire.

## For the Tincture.

Composed and set aside, this work holds an excellent certainty within contemplation; therefore, one must be steadfast in this art and attend to his work with gentleness, without any anger. One must not cease from the work once begun until he reaches the perfect end.

In this alone, every experienced practitioner—or as is customary, every researcher of this art—knows the beginning and the root of the gratitude and wisdom of this art and its operation. For whoever does not know the beginning cannot come to the work. And I will reveal this beginning to you in quite clear speech, so that you do not fail in all your undertakings: *make the fixed volatile, and [the volatile] fixed, and unless bodies are turned into bodies, and vice versa, you shall achieve nothing.* <note>original: "fac fixum Volatile fixum, et nisi fiant Corpora in Corpora, et econverso, Nihil efficies." This is a fundamental alchemical maxim: the solid must be made liquid/gaseous, and the gaseous made solid, to achieve transformation.</note>

Now, when you have rotted [the material] for the 40 days <term>$\odot$</term> <note>While the symbol $\odot$ usually represents the Sun or Gold, in this context it refers to the 40-day solar cycle of putrefaction mentioned on the previous page.</note>, take it out and open the vial again. Pour it all together into a bowl and pour distilled rainwater <term>$\nabla$</term> upon it. Draw all the salts <note>original: "Salien" / "Salia"</note> out from it very well in the most subtle way. Take great care that you draw the salts from it purely, otherwise it will all be ruined <note>original: "über ein hauffen" (literally "over a heap"); an idiom meaning to collapse or fail.</note> during sublimation; therefore, you must perform the decanting <term>abfüssig</term> with all diligence.

Now, when the salts have been poured off quite purely, place the bowl together with the material in hot, burning sand and let it dry gently. Then, put the material into a coated sublimation flask <note>A glass vessel "coated" with clay or lute to protect it from direct heat.</note>—the longer it is, the better. Place a helm <note>The "head" or cap of the distilling apparatus.</note> upon it, but do not seal it with luting <term>Verlutiert</term> <note>Luting is the airtight sealing of joints with clay or paste.</note>. Place it in a cupel <note>A shallow container, here used to hold the sand bath.</note> in sand and give it a gentle fire <term>$\Delta$</term>, so that the sand becomes only a little warm. Then, operate the fire <term>$\Delta$</term> a little [longer] <note>The symbol $♃$ (Jupiter) is used here by the scribe, likely to denote a specific duration or degree of heat.</note> and finally stronger [still], maintaining it so that the sand in the cupel glows.

When you have thus sublimated the material for 24 hours <note>original: $♃$; here used as a symbol for a full daily cycle or 24-hour period.</note>.

# The Process

When you have completed this, let it cool thoroughly. Then, take out the weighted <term>material</term> <note>original: "♎ Materi"; the symbol for Libra here refers to the measured weight of the substance.</note> and carefully place it into a bowl. Whatever remains, keep it as well; keep it until the next <term>corruption</term> <note>The "breaking down" or "rotting" phase of the alchemical process.</note> of our Stone. Then take that same mercury and dry it on warm sand. Afterward, press it through a leather cloth three or four times into a clean bowl so that no foreign matter is mixed in. At that point, it is prepared for the <term>augmentation</term> <note>The process of increasing the power or quantity of the alchemical medicine.</note>. You can perform the same process using <term>silver</term> <note>symbol: ☾</note>.

Now, take one part of such mercury (or silver) and place it into a <term>fixing glass</term> <note>An alchemical vessel designed to withstand long-term heat to "fix" volatile substances.</note> as previously illustrated—always using three parts of <unclear>lute</unclear> <note>Likely sealing clay or "Lutum Sapientiae" used to airtight the vessel.</note>. The substance will begin to rise; drive it with heat until it has completely ascended and then circulates back down. Then drive it again a little, as before, and a small amount will always remain at the bottom and begin to <term>fix</term> <note>original: "Figieren"; the process of making a volatile substance solid and resistant to heat.</note> into a mercury. You must continue this rising and circulating of the mercury until it is entirely <term>pulverized</term>, which will happen in 40 <term>days</term> <note>symbol: ☉; the sun symbol here represents a full day's cycle.</note> or at the very longest.

Once finished, you will have an eternal, never-ending <term>augmentation</term>. One part of this, made in this manner, <term>tinges</term> <note>Transmutes or "colors" a base metal into a noble one.</note> twenty parts of <term>silver</term> <note>symbol: ☾</note> or <term>copper</term> <note>symbol: ♀</note>. However, if it was made from silver, it will tinge one part to ten parts of silver or copper into fine, stable silver. But if you wish to augment the mercury further, take ten parts of its own mercury to one part...

# For the Tincture <note>original: "Pro Tinctura"</note>

Take the fixed <term>material</term> and place it into a coated clay vessel. In the same manner as before, let it be <term>fixed</term> <note>The process of making a volatile substance stable under heat.</note> and sealed for 40 days. It will then be able to <term>tinge</term> <note>To transform or transmute a base metal into a noble one.</note> at all times, increasing its power tenfold. You will notice that whenever one pound tinges 1,000 pounds, it has occurred through the repetition and the addition of one pound to <term>augment</term> it. Every time it is fixed, you must first add 10 pounds of fine <term>gold</term> <note>symbol: ☉</note> to one pound of the material, and for the second time, add 10 pounds of gold to every pound, and so on through the <term>multiplication</term> <note>The process of increasing the quantity and quality of the alchemical medicine.</note>.

However, if you wish to add <term>crude material</term> <note>original: "Crudum"; likely referring to raw, unrefined mercury.</note>, note that the first time you should add no more than half the weight of the material. Afterward, every month, add as much <term>crude mercury</term> <note>symbol: ☿ Crudi</note> as the material weighs. Fix it again in the same way as before. You may take away half of it, or as much as you wish, every month and replace it with more crude mercury, equal to the weight of the material, and let the change occur with <term>borax</term> <note>A flux used in soldering and alchemy to help metals flow and purify.</note> into a <term>body</term> <note>The solid, physical form of the metal or medicine.</note>.

And note: when you first begin with crude mercury and wish to augment it, you should only add half a pound of the <term>medicine</term> at first. But afterward, proceed every month as described above. Thus, you have a thorough report on the counsel and way of <term>augmentation</term>, which is performed upon the true, correct ground and foundation. Anything performed outside of this foundation—whether they be <term>particulars</term> <note>original: "Particularia"; chemical processes that only work on small scales or with specific metals, rather than a universal transformation.</note> or whatever they may be—are therefore lies, as all the <term>philosophers</term> <note>Refers to the "Natural Philosophers" or alchemists of antiquity and the Middle Ages.</note> say.

Now, if you wish to use the mentioned mercury for the <term>Universal</term> <note>The "Universal Medicine" or Philosopher's Stone, capable of curing all diseases and perfecting all metals.</note>, mark this <term>secret</term> <note>original: "Secretum"</note>: you must <term>weigh</term> <note>symbol: ♎︎ (Libra); in this context, it may also imply rectifying or balancing the substance through distillation seven times.</note> the mercury seven times.

# For the Tincture

Our whole operation is nothing other than the **Extraction of water** from the **Earth**, and the letting down of this water upon the Earth until the Earth **putrefies** <note>original Latin: "putrefiat"; the stage of decomposition, often called the "Black Crow," where the material must "die" to be reborn</note>. For the Earth is cleansed as it putrefies. When it has been purified, the whole **Masterpiece** <note>original Latin: "Magisterium"; the completion of the Philosopher's Stone</note> is perfected with the help of Divinity. And the **White Spirit of the Lord** was carried over the waters <note>a reference to Genesis 1:2, equating the alchemical process with the divine creation of the world</note>.

For just as in the **Creation of the World**, first the water <note>symbol: ▽</note> was present, and the Spirit of God hovered over it, so also is the beginning of this work in **sublimation** <note>the process of heating a substance until it vaporizes and then becomes solid again</note>; for it opens itself. And it continues until it has entirely <unclear>left</unclear> its body [turning] into a special transparent water <note>symbol: ▽</note> like a crystal water, which is nothing other than a vapor or steam which the fire <note>symbol: △</note> has forced, and gradually it has risen on high. The bodily matter betakes itself into the round sphere <note>symbol: ◯</note> like the stone paste; **the wind carried it in its belly** <note>original Latin: "Ventus in Ventre suo"; a famous line from the Emerald Tablet of Hermes Trismegistus</note> and elsewhere, **the soul of the Earth ascends to Heaven, and again descends to Earth and receives the power of things above and below.** But through the long action and constant, unceasing effect, it opens itself, and when caught back down, it becomes a little thicker over time. But understand that this does not happen so quickly, for the entire body must first be drawn into the height of its circle; then it begins to become thicker and more **steadfast in the fire** <note>original German: "△ frommer"; literally "fire-pious," meaning the substance can now withstand heat without vaporizing</note>. And if it should be that more of the body remains, it finally or at last consumes it so that it becomes spiritual. I say to you in Divine Truth that the Art is nothing other than to **dissolve** and **coagulate** the Stone, which happens alone through **putrefaction**.

The practitioner of our work must first **dissolve the Stone**, then **coagulate** it, because one can in no way reach perfection unless everything is changed—the Earth into water. Both of these, namely the **dissolution of the body** and the **coagulation of the spirit**, will occur in one operation; the same agent dissolves the body and coagulates the spirit—this is a **work of Nature** <note>original Latin: "opus Naturae"</note>.

## The Process

Know also that **dissolution** and **coagulation** are distinct, yet they have only one operation, namely the means: **heat**. For as soon as it has the desire, it has also immediately accomplished its operation: **coagulation**. <note>original Latin: "Coagulationem." In alchemy, dissolution (turning solid to liquid) and coagulation (liquid to solid) are the two halves of the "solve et coagula" cycle.</note> If you look diligently into the words of wisdom, you will easily be able to know it; for they have said of it that this arrangement is the **transformation of Nature** and a subtle arrangement of the natural things—heat and moisture with cold and dryness—and a marvelous mixture. <note>original Latin: "Si sapientiam Dicta diligenter in Spegeris, facile Ilam Scire poteris, De ipsa enim dixerunt quod hec Dispositio est Naturae immutatio et rerum Naturalium Calidi et humidi Cum frigido et sicco subtilis Dispositio et ad Mirabilis Commixtio."</note>

This is that which cannot be perfected by the hands [alone]. <note>original Latin: "hec est Ila quod Manibus Perfici non potest"; implying that the process is a natural or divine one that the alchemist merely facilitates.</note>

When you see here that everything below begins to stand still and no longer ascends, then Nature has accomplished the **conjunction**. For the moisture has become denser, as the elements along with the soul, by means of the spirit, find the **spiritual body** <note>original German: "Spiritualischen Corper"; the state where matter has been purified and "spiritualized" so it can be transformed.</note> back together as one. This is an **incombustible oil** <note>original Latin: "oleum Incompositibile"; a substance that fire cannot destroy or decompose.</note>. And if you were to throw a glowing piece of <term>gold</term> <note>symbol: ☉ (the Sun or Gold)</note> into this oil, it would immediately become <term>gold</term> <note>symbol: ☉</note>. However, it is not necessary to make your purchase <insert>to perform this test</insert> yet if you wish to have your work completed. For know that this oil no longer leaves its various parts, because the <term>gold</term> <note>symbol: ☉</note> is nothing other than **fixed, prepared oil**, so that no consumption can happen to it in the <term>fire</term> <note>symbol: △ (Fire)</note>. Therefore, the extracted firmness of the oil is a **Tincture**; for firmness belongs to the soul, which exhales itself with great difficulty, or very slowly and subtly, just as all the philosophers write.

Its complexion is temperate and its nature is directed in **heat, cold, moisture, and dryness**; neither is there anything superfluous in it, nor anything diminished in its essence. Let air nourish the fire, just as water [nourishes] the earth. In alchemy, "killing" or "mortifying" a substance means stripping it of its volatile or changing qualities to make it fixed and stable.</note>

### For the Tincture

In its fire [🜂], it flows upon its own fiery [🜂-like] nature to ignite itself. And therein penetrates that water which was hidden in its interior from the beginning. And thus water and air are the cause of retaining the tincture—the water and air [held] in the oil against combustion. <note>original Latin: "et sic est causa retinendi Tincturam aqua et aerem in oleum a Combustione." Alchemists believed that for a substance to resist being destroyed by fire, it needed a perfect balance of moisture and air to "buffer" the heat.</note> And the oil is the cause of retaining the tincture, the moisture which is the cause of the appearance of the colors. And so the material here will be brought from its present state into the subtle state, and the water [🜄] will struggle with the fire [🜂] and endure the same.

And thus you understand well; here lies the whole of our philosophy. <note>original Latin: "et sic bene intelligis, hic iacet tota Nostra philosophica."</note> It is to be noted that in the hidden [interior] of our **Stone** there is heat and dryness, and in the manifest [exterior] there is coldness and moisture. <note>Alchemical theory often used the terms "occulto" (hidden/inner) and "manifesto" (outward/visible). The goal was often to "turn the inside out," making the inner heat become the outer reality.</note> Wherefore it is necessary that its manifest part be hidden. The heat which is in the hidden part is the element of oil, which is its [own] coldness and dryness; the fire tints it. That which is manifest, however, is coldness and moisture; it is therefore necessary to have a proportion between these, so that the coldness and moisture are tempered by the heat and dryness that were in the hidden.

Indeed, that coldness and moisture is a watery and scorching smoke which corrupts and gives birth to blackness. <note>original Latin: "nigredinem." This refers to the *nigredo* or "black stage," the first phase of the Great Work representing decomposition or "the death of the matter."</note> And that **Stone** is of one virtue and nature in the hidden, and another in the manifest; but in a complete mixture, it is of the same virtue and nature. And thus the most noble spirit is changed; thereafter it becomes flowing and an oil, which is a **Tincture** that is truly multiplicative, consolidating, coloring, purifying, and confirming. <note>original Latin: "Multiplicativa, Consolidativa, Colorativa, Purgativa, et Confirmativa." A multiplicative tincture is one that can transform a large amount of base metal into gold with only a small amount of the medicine.</note>

Note that this oil, in an earthly manner, stays above the water [🜄], and when it begins to thicken, it falls gracefully and slowly to the bottom. When the color is just like a lily stalk or like bright pomegranate seeds, then know that you should continue without ceasing to govern the vaporous parts well. <note>Color changes were the primary indicators of progress in an alchemical experiment. The "lily" often refers to a white stage, while "pomegranate" suggests the deep red of the final stage.</note> And do not exceed the fifth [degree] of inability, as you will be taught hereafter regarding the Sun [☉/Gold]. And finally, when the fixation begins, a little cap will form from the Sun [☉/Gold]. <note>original German: "Häublin," a diminutive for "hood" or "cap." This refers to a crust or film forming on the surface of the molten metal or chemical mixture, signaling the start of "fixation" (the process where volatile substances become solid and heat-resistant).</note>

## The Process

Regarding the power and perfection of the philosophers'. After the perfection is achieved, the power [of the Stone] cannot enter into any metal—neither perfect nor imperfect bodies—without a **Medium** <note>original: "Mittl." In alchemy, a "medium" or "flux" is a substance added to help the Stone "tinge" or penetrate the dense structure of a metal.</note>. For the entry must happen through this medium. Even if the **Medicine** <note>Another name for the Philosopher's Stone.</note> were to act upon a metal without the medium, and you left it in a vessel for ten years, it would not accept the aforementioned medium because of its [the Medicine's] great purity. It acts, however, like <term>Gold</term> <note>original symbol: $\odot$</note> in the <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: $\triangle$</note>.

And mark well this great secret as just mentioned: the Medicine is the **woman’s member** <note>An alchemical metaphor describing the Medicine as the receptive, feminine principle that must "embrace" the masculine substance to be effective.</note> and does not let go of that which surrounds it. For when they are joined, the Medicine is so penetrating that it goes right through the <term>crucible</term> <note>original symbol: $\mathcal{T}$, a "test" or melting pot designed to withstand high heat.</note>. Finally, when it has been inside for three hours, let it cool by itself; then break the crucible and take it out. It will be a pearl, like a glass, which is still a Medicine.

One pound of this Medicine acts upon 1,000 pounds of <term>Tin</term> <note>original symbol: $\mathcal{4}$</note> or <term>Lead</term> <note>original symbol: $\hbar$</note>. When it is combined, it **tinctures** <note>To "tinge" or tincture is to permanently change the color and nature of a substance.</note> all 1,000 pounds into eternally fine, stable Gold. However, should the result be brittle <note>original: "Ungeschmeidig," meaning the metal is not malleable or "soft" enough to be worked by a smith.</note>, once you have thrown the Medicine in, keep it for five hours in a <term>sand bath</term> <note>original: "r : a :" or *remora arenae*.</note> in a semicircular vessel <note>original: "Halgreis," likely *Halbkreis*.</note> with a stirring rod in the crucible. Whatever sticks to the rod, strike it upon an **anvil**; you will soon see in the Gold if it is still brittle or not.

If you find it to still be brittle, add more Tin or <term>Copper</term> <note>original symbol: $\mathcal{Q}$</note> to that which you have set out to tincture; then it will become fine and malleable. And mark well this aforementioned secret regarding this [process]. Reveal this to no human being; write it upon the tablet of your heart so that the ungodly, proud, and haughty may not reach a successful end. Remember that all of this is a **gift of God**, and if you reveal it, you shall see that God will punish you for it.
