# The Process

As in the beginning, so also at the end: once it is accomplished and it gives off no smoke upon <term>Lead</term> <note>original symbol: $\square$. In this context, it likely refers to a cupellation test where the medicine is tested on lead to see if it remains stable under heat.</note>, and you have whatever you need for <term>Gold</term> <note>original symbol: $\odot$ (Sol).</note>, then work your <term>Medicine</term> toward the pure preparation of <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: $\unicode{x263F}$.</note>. However, for the further preparation of the Gold Tincture, you must proceed in the same way with 1,000 <term>pounds</term> <note>original symbol: $\unicode{x2114}$ (Libra).</note> of <term>Calx of Gold</term> <note>A powder produced by heating a metal until it oxidizes or breaks down.</note> to 1 pound of Medicine. These are to be rubbed together upon a <term>glass grinding stone</term> <note>original symbol: $\unicode{x260A}$ Glaser Reibstein. A smooth stone used for the fine pulverization of alchemical ingredients.</note> which must be very fine and subtle. Place this into a well-<term>luted</term> <note>Sealed with "lute," a specialized airtight clay or cement used to prevent vapors from escaping.</note> <term>vessel</term> <note>original symbol: $\unicode{x2603}$.</note>, and leave it for 3 <term>intervals</term> <note>original symbol: $\square$. This likely refers to "hours" or a specific "philosophical day" in the heating cycle.</note> in every measure, just as you were previously taught regarding the white Medicine of Mercury. Then let it glow, and afterwards let it sit for another 3 intervals. In this way, the Medicine unites with the <term>Antimony</term> <note>original symbol: $\unicode{x2641}$. In this context, it may represent the "Earth of Gold" or a specific metallic primer.</note> of Gold, drawing it toward and into itself. It remains brittle and shatters like glass; this is the very first stage of preparing the <term>Body</term> <note>The physical metal being transformed.</note> for the Tincture.

From such brittle Medicine: take 1 pound and cast it upon 1,000 pounds of coagulated Mercury or <term>Copper</term> <note>original symbol: $\unicode{x2640}$ (Venus).</note>. Once it is coagulated, or if it is in Mercury alone, cast 1 pound of the brittle Medicine upon it and let it stand for 3 intervals in the <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: $\triangle$.</note>. Reach in with a gold wire and observe if the result begins to appear; if it is still un-malleable <note>original: "Ungeschmidig." Meaning the metal is too brittle to be hammered or worked.</note>, then draw in even more coagulated Mercury or Copper, as mentioned before. Continue testing with the wire until the "Seed" can endure the process. When you see that it is no longer [brittle] but malleable, pour it all together into an <term>ingot-mold</term> <note>original: "Inguß." A mold used for casting metal into bars or shapes.</note>. Thus you have good, constant Gold, which is one degree higher than that which Nature gives in the Earth; namely, it has 25 carats <note>Pure gold is traditionally 24 carats; 25 carats signifies a "supernatural" purity achieved through alchemy.</note>.

Thus you have accomplished the praiseworthy, divine, and blessed Art with the help of Nature—from one thing, and in one glass, also in one furnace, and with one Fire. Herewith are all philosophical steps along with the blessed Work accomplished and perfected. Praise, prize, and honor be to God from eternity to eternity.

# For the Tincture
## What Follows Concerning the Furnace

Now I will tell you about the furnace: how large, high, and wide it must be, and what kind of <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: $\triangle$. The triangle is the standard alchemical shorthand for the element of fire.</note> you should lay within it, and how you should govern that same philosophical Fire.

The <term>Rosary</term> <note>original: "Rosarius dicit." A water bath used to provide a steady, temperate heat that does not exceed the boiling point of water.</note> fail, since its use is also very temperate. Whence Alchidius <note>An authority often cited in alchemical texts, sometimes identified as a philosopher or a corruption of "Al-Kindi."</note> says: "In what fire should you cook? I will show you." Our fire is a hidden thing, in moist horse dung; it is a wise, moist fire in the first degree, whose property is not to destroy the oil of the matter, but to increase it because of its temperate humidity. That equal and temperate heat is highly necessary in the generation of this art.

The furnace shall be made nine man’s feet long and five high. In the middle shall be the round hearth; the second part should be twice as wide as the other. Specifically, each internal chamber <note>original: "dach," literally "roof," but here referring to the compartments or tiers inside the furnace.</note> should be four <term>inches</term> <note>original: "furch." Likely an archaic measurement or a variant of "furrow," here implying a specific width relative to the furnace's scale.</note> wide and a half-inch high—then it has the correct size, which may then be called a true philosophical furnace. Fill such compartments with horse dung, ensuring it is packed well. When they are full, let them stand thus; and from the middle, bury the <term>Matter</term> <note>The alchemical substance undergoing transformation.</note> within, just as you were taught earlier in the <term>Practice</term> <note>Refers to the practical, hands-on instructions (the *Practica*) provided in the earlier pages of the manuscript.</note>. One part you must renew with new, fresh horse dung; namely, in the middle, you must remove the burnt-out dung from top to bottom, about a good hand's-breadth from the bottom of the furnace, and fill it with fresh dung as said above, without lighting it. On the third day, it reaches its proper warmth. And when it has stood thus for <term>two and a half hours</term> <note>original: "Drithalb stunt." An archaic German expression meaning "the third half," or two and a half.</note>, make a hole so that

## Process

The <term>Sun</term> <note>original symbol: $\odot$. In alchemy, this represents Gold or the solar essence of the Stone.</note> should be placed inside; set it right in the middle of the manure. And from that same hour, the other part [of the furnace] should be cleared of the aforementioned manure in the same manner as before. Throw fresh manure into that place and let it stand for two and a half hours <note>original: "drithalb Stund." In early modern German, this specific construction means "the third half," or 2.5.</note> to begin heating. Then, the <term>Sun</term> is placed within it, and the other part is renewed just as before. In this way, every 15 days, a glowing red part of the furnace comes into use, which is called: *Cook, and cook again* <note>original: "Coque, et iterum Coque." A fundamental alchemical maxim emphasizing that the secret of the Work lies in the patient, repeated application of heat.</note>.

Note well that you must always continue on the side where you began; take heed of such <unclear>odol</unclear> <note>The word is difficult to read; it likely refers to the "oil" or essence being produced.</note> so that you maintain it with the renewal, as has been frequently mentioned above. And when you now wish to "corrupt" <note>In alchemy, "corruption" is not a negative term; it refers to the breaking down of a substance's form so that it can be "generated" or reborn into a higher state.</note> the metals, you must take a phial as mentioned in the *Practica* <note>Likely referring to a specific practical manual or a preceding section of this manuscript.</note>, which has a long neck and is sealed by melting, as follows: for the neck of the phial must extend out from the top a little, approximately 12 finger-widths <note>original: "Zwerchfinger." A traditional measurement based on the width of a finger.</note> or a hand-breadth.

However, if you are purging <note>Refining or purifying.</note> our <term>Antimony</term> <note>original symbol: $\earth$. While this symbol often represents Earth or Vitriol, in this context of metallic processing, it frequently denotes Antimony.</note> and wish to set it with the sphere into its proper place or allotted passage, then the wide part that lies upon the manure needs no hole; the more precisely it rests upon it, the better it is. And note that you should set our <term>Antimony</term> together with the silver sphere right in the middle of the manure, and surround it on all sides with manure. Also, on each part of the furnace, a thick layer of straw is laid over the manure. Close it so precisely that it hardly moves; thus the vaporous things remain in the <term>sinus</term> <note>original: "sino." This refers to the interior cavity or "hollow" of the vessel where the vapors circulate.</note>. This is now the philosophical furnace and <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: $\triangle$.</note>, which must be managed in this specific way from beginning to end.

# For the Tincture <note>original: "Pro Tinctura." A tincture is a concentrated alchemical substance believed to have the power to transmute metals or heal the body.</note>

Therefore, learn herein, and pray to God for wisdom and understanding, and also that He may come to your aid at the beginning of this high and praiseworthy art, for the praise of God and the improvement of your neighbor, helping you happily with His divine blessing.

# Dialogue

...received as a gift of the mind <note>original: *mentischen gabe*; likely referring to an intellectual or divinely inspired understanding rather than a physical object.</note>, with all friendliness all the days that I have lived. From the time I began to research this noble **Art** <note>Alchemy was frequently referred to as the "Noble Art" or "Sacred Art."</note>, I have always begun with a perfect heart to pray for the **Solution of the Philosophers** <term>Solution</term> <note>The process of dissolving a solid into a liquid, often considered the first essential step in the Great Work.</note>. And I have obtained such [understanding], as far as was possible, from no living person. And now I know everything concerning the understanding: that all those who work [at this Art] in the whole world are full of error, and are blinded in their evil ignorance. 

For some work in **Gold** <term>☉</term>, some in **Silver** <term>☽</term>, some in **Borax** <note>original: *Borasiö*</note>, some in human bone, and some in eggs, some in water, sheep <note>original: *Schaffen*; likely referring to sheep’s wool or other animal materials used by "puffers" or false alchemists.</note>, **Marcasites** <note>A common mineral (iron sulfide) often mistaken for gold or silver ore.</note> and the like. From all these, I—and also your Grace—recognize that the **Tincture** <term>Tinctur</term> <note>The potent substance capable of transforming base metals into gold or healing the body.</note> of our **Stone** is extracted alone from the **Mercury of the Wise** <term>☿</term>, which is not the common mercury, and not that which is drawn from the earth or dug out of it (though they also call that mercury). 

Rather, our **Mercury** is from the **Body, Soul, and Spirit**. And you, my Master, have taught me at the beginning of this little book; and behold, in all the world there is no other thing, but only this **Stone**, and it alone is known. And dear Master, whatever [by] your dignity and power is lacking in me, in the hope that I might be pleasing to God and serve you with recompense, that I will gladly do and be of service to you.

**Master:** Dear son, I seek nothing from you, but only that you love God your Lord with all your heart and with all your soul, He who has revealed this great **Mastery** to you through me. And be faithful and cautious in all your works, so that you do not become unjust or unworthy, as you have written. And if you do so, then I commend you to the care of the Lord. And give God the honor, for He is a sustainer and the source <note>original: *Versprung*; a variation of *Ursprung* (origin/source).</note> of all good, and in Him shall be kept all glory and wisdom. May His name be blessed from world to world [forever], Amen.

To Almighty God be praise, honor, and glory forever and ever, Amen. <note>original Latin: *Deo omnipotenti sit Laus honor et gloria in seculorum secula Amen.*</note>

->Glory to God alone<-

# Example of the Philosophical Art.

## An Example of the Philosophers' Art.

A noble cry: death in the body! The natures are ignobly joined and united—the Earth of **Water** <term>$\nabla$</term> <note>original: *$\nabla$*; the symbol for the element of Water.</note> to its **Fire** <term>$\Delta$</term> <note>original: *$\Delta$*; the symbol for the element of Fire.</note>. And all are in **Saturn** <term>$\hbar$</term> <note>original: *$\hbar$*; the symbol for the planet/metal Saturn or Lead, often representing the "black" stage of decay in alchemy.</note>; with these, the locks of the Art are opened, as Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure considered the father of alchemy.</note> and his predecessors say. From the Stone that hangs over the sea, there is an old opinion: a Child <note>The "Philosophical Child" or *Filius Philosophorum* is a common symbol for the completed Philosopher's Stone.</note>—his name is called wonderful above all—with whom he kills the living and quickens the dead things. And he holds life and death, and this, and the going out and coming in; with him, you shall possess the Art.

In which the Arabs <note>A reference to the medieval Arabic alchemical tradition (like Geber or Rhazes) from which much Western alchemy was derived.</note> become one through drying; I have told you the truth by the Creator of the Stone of Paradise. The light of life is in it; two contrary things are joined together, namely **Fire** <term>$\Delta$</term> and **Water** <term>$\nabla$</term>. This makes the house living, and this kills it; this and the **Sun** <term>$\odot$</term> <note>original: *$\odot$*; the symbol for the Sun or Gold.</note> [give] their life, joined together by Him who is life and death.

I lie not; I have told you the truth. And gum coagulates our milk, and milk dissolves our gum <note>A poetic description of the alchemical "solve et coagula" (dissolve and congeal) process using the metaphors of "gum" (solid) and "milk" (liquid).</note>; and thereafter comes its oriental redness and brightness. Whosoever receives this Stone—found without stench, and without the highest counsel or help—through it, the philosophers are made great and exalted above all others, and have prophesied things to come. I have told you the truth by the power of Heaven, of which I have knowingly not lied. Our Old Man is our old Frank <note>original: *Franck*; possibly a proper name or a corruption of a technical term, or referring to "free/pure" matter.</note>; this is then his head with his tail <note>A reference to the Ouroboros, the serpent eating its own tail, symbolizing the cyclical nature of the work.</note>, and the head is the soul, and the spirit is made out of clay <note>original: *Leimer*; likely meaning *Lehm* (clay or loam), referencing the "Adamie" or earthly matter.</note>.

# On the Stone

The subtle part of <term>Nature<note>original: *Natur*. In alchemy, "Nature" often refers to the inherent power or life-force within a substance that allows it to grow or change.</note></term> that is within it, that is the spirit; and that same spirit shall <term>tinge<note>original: *tingieren*. The spirit does not stop subduing the material until it brings it into its own nature, for it makes a spirit out of the <term>body<note>original: *Corpus*.</note></term>. For our <term>Stone<note>The Philosophers' Stone, the legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold.</note></term>, in the first place, kills itself, and <term>dissolves<note>original: *solviert*.</note></term> itself, and <term>coagulates<note>original: *covaguliert*. And the <term>philosophers<note>original: *philosophi*. This refers to the ancient and medieval alchemists.</note></term> say that one finds sixteen in <term>Mercury<note>original: ☿. Therefore, there is nothing more than one thing, which the philosophers call <term>Living Mercury<note>original: *☿ Vivum*. And this is our <term>Water<note>original: 🜄.</note></term> which <term>calcinates<note>original: *calciniert*. To reduce a metal to a fine powder through heat or chemical action.</note></term> our <term>body of antimony<note>original: *Corpus 🜍*. And yet, it is not "water" according to the [common] nature of the work; it makes the <term>bodies</term> alive; nature possesses this <term>Water</term>.

# Chapter Three: Concerning the Stone.

Now note that the beginning of this matter consists of two things: that is, the <term>Mercury of the Philosophers<note>symbol: ☿. Alchemists distinguished "philosophical" mercury—a pure, life-giving essence—from the common liquid metal mercury.</note></term> and <term>Fire<note>symbol: △</note></term>. And yet it is not common mercury, nor common fire, neither in their nature nor in their substance; for in these things the four <term>elements<note>The traditional building blocks: Earth, Air, Fire, and Water.</note></term> are visible, and the wise recognize them by their virtues and create from them their art and mastery—[namely] <term>Fire<note>symbol: △</note></term> and <term>Mercury<note>symbol: ☿</note></term>, of which they speak and write for <term>tinctures<note>Substances capable of transmuting and coloring base metals.</note></term> or for <term>transmuting<note>original: *Tingieren*. To "tinge" or dye a metal, signifying its inner transformation.</note></term>.

Therefore Richard of <unclear>Strafford</unclear><note>original: *Richardus d' Straf*. # On the Stone <note>original Latin: *De Lapide*</note>

[of the] philosophers <note>original Latin header: *philosophorum*</note>

This is what the speech of the philosopher in the **Assembly** <note>original: *Turba* [Philosophorum]—a famous medieval alchemical text featuring a debate among ancient sages</note> says: unless our **ore** <term>Ertz—raw mineral material</term> is colored, it does not color [anything else]. But when it is colored, then it also colors. Another philosopher says: Our ore does not **tincture** <term>tingieren—to dye or fundamentally transform the nature of a metal</term> unless it is first tinctured itself. Therefore, the tincturing **venom** <note>original: *venenum*—in alchemy, this refers to a potent, transformative spirit or "sting" rather than a simple poison</note> does not come out of our ore unless it is prepared for tincturing. This chapter is proven from the true [teachings] and speech of the philosophers.

If our ore cannot be broken down by any kind of **governance** <term>Regierung—the controlled application of heat and process</term>, so that nothing can enter into it, then it can also tincture nothing. For all colors are enclosed within it for its **perfection**. For it cannot give off its colors as long as it remains in its raw nature; rather, its colors are diminished. Therefore, it must be tinctured with such governance and with such colors that are superior to it. The governance is that it be tinctured through the manifold colors of the **burnt blood** <note>original: *geprandt Bludts*—likely referring to a deep red state or iron oxide powder</note>, which then, through its overflow into the coloring process, when cast upon another metal, tinctures it into true **Gold** <term>☉ <note>symbol for Gold</note></term> and incomparable **tincture** and **fixity** <note>term: *Fixiheit*—the ability of a substance to remain stable and not evaporate in the heat of the fire</note>. This is because of its virtue and fixity, which it has attained through the **regimen** <note>original: *Regiment*—the stages of the alchemical process</note> and from tincturing things.

### Chapter Twelve <note>original Latin: *Caput duodecimum*</note>

**T**herefore, the power and virtue of the **Elixir** is such that, through the virtuous nature it has received from Nature and from Art, it is powerful enough to drive out all impurity and to tincture all **imperfect bodies** <note>original: *Imperfecte Corpora*—base metals like lead or tin</note> placed in the fire into true **Gold** <term>☉ <note>symbol for Gold</note></term>. It is also powerful enough to make people healthy and bring them into their balanced **quality** <note>original: *Qualitet*—referring to the balance of the four humors or temperaments in the body</note>.

But whoever does not understand this book should not blame the sages, but rather himself, on account of his own ignorance.

Therefore I give thanks to the **Eternal Wisdom** <note>often referring to the personified "Sophia," representing divine insight</note> which has granted me the strength and understanding to write of this great treasure, and which I have preserved for our sons, through the true riches of the philosophers and all the sages. May the name of that Eternal Wisdom be blessed, praised, and honored, now and for eternal times.

# The Red Man. 4

Naturally, Water <note>original symbol: 🜄</note> drives everything into itself through the mixing, right down to the bottom. And after that, let it remain in its proven place, well-sealed so that nothing escapes. Keep a moderate heat with you, as was mentioned before, so that the black-red [matter] partly becomes white. After that, drive it out again as it has become, and grind it again, and <term>imbibe</term> <note>original: *Imbibiers*; the alchemical process of adding liquid to a solid to nourish or soften it.</note> it, and work it once more.

Do this 41 times; in this way, you have purified the black earth to such a degree and with such virtue that through the power of Fire <note>original symbol: 🜂</note>, the matter becomes entirely white. Keep this same matter beautiful, for it is the white dust from the <term>Black Raven</term> <note>original: *schwartzen Rappen*; a symbol for the *nigredo* or "blackness" stage of alchemy, representing the death or decomposition of the starting material.</note>, as you have heard before.

For you have found a great treasure, and it is called a "White Earth" of the Water <note>original symbol: 🜄</note>, or the "Dust of the Grain of Lead." Therefore, Master <term>Morienes</term> <note>Morienus, a legendary 7th-century hermit and alchemist famous for his dialogues on the philosopher's stone.</note> says and speaks: "The Earth filed with its Water, and when this is done, the entire mastery is completed."

Also, in the joining and the operation, there occurs the first composition of the four elements. For when they are joined together, the element of Water requires the element of Fire, and the element of Air [requires] the element of Earth. There, the Man and the Woman who were alone are joined together.

Also, there are joined together the Sun <note>original symbol: ☉; representing Gold</note>, the Moon <note>original symbol: ☽; representing Silver</note>, and the Earth <note>original symbol: 🜃</note>.

Also, there occurs a refreshing of the dead bodies. Now you have planted the White Earth and prepared what you previously desired: to keep the <term>Ursas</term> <note>original: *Ursas*; likely a corruption of the Latin *ousia* (essence) or *ursis* (basis), referring here to the foundational root or "starter" of the stone.</note> or the Ferment <note>original: *Fermenti*; a substance added to a process to trigger a transformation, much like yeast in bread.</note>, which is a confirmation of our Stone. Therefore the philosophers say: "It softens before our Earth," which you sow therein, or [from which] you are the source.

And the nature of Fire <note>original symbol: Δ</note> is nature, from which the four elements [arise]. And the entire effectiveness will be accomplished within itself, and there is no need for any kind of manual handling except for our sublimation, which must happen seven times.

Afterward, balance <note>original symbol: ♎</note> the body with our sublimation seven times, as is recorded above, which returns to a First Matter as was previously indicated. It coagulates, sublimates, and distills itself; it purely calcines itself, so that <margin>there is enough</margin> of it before the start. And after that, it shall be transformed into the 4 elements; then you will find what you seek: the Fire and Water <note>original symbols: Δ|∇</note> out of the earth.

Therefore, do not burn away its flowers <term>flores: the crystalline sublimate that rises to the top of the vessel</term>. You will also [see] that the precursor is your key to the whole work. After the precursor, the Queen appears; she is transformed through the Fire <note>original symbol: Δ</note> into a new King; then the King is born.

## A Secret Poem

It is a <term>lowly</term> <note>original: schrödes; meaning base, common, or of little value; the alchemists often claimed their secret ingredient was something discarded or found on any dungheap</note> thing, which is yet found everywhere, and is born of the four elements. And do not think that it is false, but rather true and certain, in all testimony true and righteous as if it were of God, and the true divinity itself. And the honor and the praise be to God the Lord, from eternity to eternity, Amen.

The virtue and virtuousness of the <term>Stone</term> <note>The Philosopher's Stone</note> lies in the appetitive, powerful, and rational virtues to heal all sicknesses beyond all medicine; for it gladdens the heart, increases strength, and preserves virtue. # A beautiful poem

This Art is but a single thing,
It holds much clever cunning within,
And signifies the **Stone**,
Of the clever and wise alone.

...if it will not dissolve, make it diligently into **Gold** <note>symbol: $\odot$</note> and thereafter into **Oil** <note>symbol: °o°</note>. This is spoken through a parable; if you are a philosopher, you will well understand what is meant by this.

## Concerning the Oil of the Philosophers

The Oil of the Philosophers—that is, the oil extracted from the four elements and which was discovered or invented by a thousand masters—now that this great secret has been revealed, no man may attain the **Philosopher’s Stone** unless he possesses a key with which to unlock the Oil of the Philosophers. It is an oil, and it exists together with **Fire** <note>original Latin: Igni</note>; the body suffers great distress before the soul is separated from it.

<term>Arnaldus de Villa Nova</term> <note>A celebrated 13th-century physician and alchemist.</note> says: In the discovery of <term>Antimony</term> <note>symbol: ♁</note> lies half the art, or spoken another way, moderate experience. For there, the **Fire** <note>symbol: $\Delta$</note> in the dissolution or <term>solution</term> <note>original: solution</note> should be light and gentle; in the second solution, moderate; in the **Coagulation** <note>The process of thickening or solidifying a liquid.</note>, properly tempered; in the **Whitening** <note>original: Albatio; the *albedo* stage of the Great Work.</note>, strong; and in the **Reddening** <note>original: Rubification; the *rubedo* or final stage of the Great Work.</note>, a strong fire <note>symbol: $\Delta$</note>. However, if you err in this governance and temperament according to the degrees of the fire, you will without doubt lament your labor and loss with mournful sighs.

Therefore, it is necessary that you apply yourself well to your work. The skill of the senses is half the hidden art, as is the art of the senses; therefore, you should pay attention only to the completion of perfection.

## True Preparation of Mercury

Notable things regarding our Antimony: Take <note>symbol: $\mathcal{R}_{\text{x}}$</note> Antimony, or the "Lesser Minerals."

### Philosophical Miscellany

It is not **Gold** <term>☉</term> that is the fire, neither in its own nature nor in the nature or power that the earth provides; rather, it is that which the Art and Mastery provides. Likewise also with **Silver** <term>☽</term>, of which they speak little. You should know that the ancients found nothing intelligible in the natural earth or in those metals which they did not find in **Mercury** <term>☿</term> and its nature, and in the **Antimony** <term>♁</term> <note>While this symbol often represents the planet Earth, in this alchemical context it likely refers to Antimony or the "Philosophical Earth" used as a base</note> that was coagulated within it.

Several Masters speak of three different things; for assistance they call it **Mercury** <term>☿</term>, and for assistance they call it **Antimony** <term>♁</term>. Yet all Masters say that it is but one single thing, and in that thing are all four elements, which can be visibly separated. Those who are wise can extract them quite naturally, and it becomes a **Pure Stone**.

You should know that the **Tincture** <note>the medicinal or transformative essence sought by alchemists</note> is born and made from a fluid **matter** <note>original: *Materia*</note> from which a smoke <note>or vapor</note> arises and ascends into the upper part of the **alembic** <term>⚗</term> <note>a pear-shaped distilling vessel</note>. There, the subtle part becomes hard and **fixed** <note>original: *figiert*; "fixation" refers to making a volatile substance stable and resistant to heat</note>. You should know that no red part can come to be unless you have first drawn it from the elements that are pure and clear white, which are equally eternal and constant. For the whiteness that is seen there is the purification of the work; afterward comes the redness, for the redness is the entirety of the Art and the whole power of the work. When the redness increases, grows, and rises, the more it becomes fixed; for in the redness is the highest **fixation** <note>original: *Figierung*</note>. The redness is the bringing-to-life; the entire power and Art consists of raising and increasing the redness, for therein lies the fixed constancy. O God, through Your gentleness You give the Art so mildly; O, study is pleasant! I say this with a faithful spirit, just as God [acts] through His great mercy.

# AVICENNA'S SEVEN RULES <note>original: *AVICENAE SEPTEM REGVlae*</note>
->from which the **Philosopher's Stone** <note>original: *Lapis philosophorum*</note> is composed<-

### 1. Rule
The first operation is that the noblest substance that exists, being subtle and pure, must be extracted from the **matter** <note>the raw material or "prima materia" used at the start of the work</note>.

### 2. Rule
The **matter** or **subject** <note>the physical substance being worked upon</note> must be dissolved into water.

### 3. Rule
**Putrefaction** <term>Putrefactio</term> <note>the stage of "rotting" or breaking down, essential for rebirth</note> must precede **generation** <note>the birth of the new, perfected substance</note>; for the philosophers say that the destruction of one thing is the birth of another.

### 4. Rule
This is the **whitening** <term>Albatio</term> <note>also known as Albedo</note>; for it is necessary that the gathered, coarse matter be washed and purified from all corrupting impurity. However, the philosophers say that the longer the **water** <note>original: <image-desc>alchemical symbol for water (inverted triangle)</image-desc></note> remains over the **earth** <note>the solid material at the bottom of the vessel</note>, the more it is washed.

## 5. Rule <note>original: *Regula*</note>
**Coagulation** <term>Coagulatio</term> <note>the process of making a liquid or dissolved substance solid</note> follows, for our **Sun** <note>original: ☉; representing Gold or the masculine principle of the Work</note> must be dried out into earth by gentle warmth and the cooking of our Sun, and become an **Antimony** <note>original: ♁; the symbol for antimony or the Earth, representing the fixed, solid state</note>.

## 6. Rule
Thereafter it must be **calcined** <term>Calcinatio</term> <note>heating a substance to a high temperature to reduce it to a powder or ash</note>, for it is known that calcined matter is more suitable for our **Work** <note>original: *Werck*; the alchemical process of creating the Philosopher's Stone</note> than the ancestors were; there are several philosophers who maintain that **calcination** is exactly the same as **fixation** <term>Fixatio</term> <note>the process of making a volatile substance stable so it no longer evaporates when heated</note>. In this they do not speak wrongly, because both these paths proceed through **sublimation** <term>Sublimatio</term> <note>the process where a solid is heated into a vapor and then collected again as a solid to purify it</note>.

## 7. Rule
Know how to **bury** <note>referring to Inhumation, the process of placing the matter in a dark, warm environment for incubation</note>, so that our whole **Work** may be completed in a <unclear>white</unclear> <note>original: *Weiße*</note> in one **vessel** <note>original: *geschier*</note>; and everything goes into one, from one, and out of one.

## Table of the Lord’s Great Knowledge <note>original: *Tabula des Herrn grosen Wissens*</note>

Initially, the true matter and color must be placed in our **Green Lion** <term>Green Lion</term> <note>a term for a powerful solvent, often acidic, used to break down metals</note>. For the 4th step, there follows the **sinking** <note>original: *Senkung*; the settling of solid particles</note>, which is spoken of greatly in the first days and is called **Fire** <note>original: △</note>.

For the 5th step, it is white to see that the greatest part of our **Mercury** <note>original: ☿</note> turns into earth—hard, strong, and vast land.

For the 6th step, one also observes how the hard earth, which initially stood atop the **Water** <note>original: ▽</note>, gradually settles to the bottom of the **vessel** <note>original: *geschirrs*</note>.

For the 7th step, one must learn how the **Water** <note>original: ▽</note> becomes **Mercury** <note>original: ☿</note>, which is then called **Oil of the Philosophers** <note>original: *oleum philosophorum*</note>.

For the 9th step, the **Mercury** <note>original: ☿</note> is completely purified of its hardness; it remains milk-colored and appears milk-colored in **Hell**.

For the 10th step, watch how the sharp mists in the vessel settle down into the **Body** <note>original: *Corpus*</note> from which they had risen.

For the 11th step, notice how from the ashes a white glint appears, like a **shining marble**; that is the **White Elixir** <note>original: *Elixir zu dem Weißen*</note>, and it has become a <unclear>solid</unclear> <note>original: *lichen*; possibly referring to the *leiche* or body of the matter</note>.

Finally, the completion appears: the white changes into a glistening, transparent **Red**, transformed like a **Ruby**. This is the **Red Elixir** <note>original: *Elixir ad Rubrum*</note>. And if you wish to understand this Art correctly, then read it part by part, and you will experience wonders.

# TREATISE
## ON THE FIFTH
### ESSENCE
#### OF WINE

Firstly, take in the name of God clear Roman wine, or another clear wine that has been drawn from the mother <note>original: *Mutter*; the lees or sediment at the bottom of the wine cask</note>, for there must be no cloudiness in it at all. For the Philosophers say one must draw our wine into its own self <note>original: *in d auch ein ding ziehen*; likely referring to an enclosed distillation process</note> without adding any foreign substance. Thus, use pure, clear wine that is of good smell and taste; from this, its four elements are to be separated as much as possible. 

For to perfectly separate the elements—namely, to extract the **Air** <note>original symbol: $\triangle$; the text describes it as hot and moist</note> from the **Fire** <note>original symbol: $\triangle$; the text describes it as hot and dry</note> at the same time—is impossible. Because **Air** is hot and moist, one cannot perfectly separate the moisture from the heat. And **Water** <note>original symbol: $\nabla$</note> is cold and moist; one cannot perfectly separate the cold from the moisture. Similarly, **Fire** is hot and dry; one cannot separate the heat from the dryness. Therefore, it is impossible to separate the elements cleanly from one another; instead, they would remain jumbled together. For in every element there are two natures: one is manifest <note>outwardly visible</note> and the other is secret <note>hidden within</note>. For example, **Water** is cold and moist; the moisture...

# Concerning the Fifth Essence of Wine

Therefore, Aristotle says, just as you have <term>water</term> <note>original: symbol $\nabla$</note> from the **Air**, and the **Air** from <term>fire</term> <note>original: symbol $\Delta$</note>, and that <term>fire</term> <note>original: symbol $\Delta$</note> from the **Earth**, and have then perfectly separated these from all impurity, you then possess the Right Art. Then take a wonderfully beautiful vessel—the larger the better—and put your **air** <note>referring to the distilled spirit or "breath" of the wine</note> into it. Distill it thus with this heat until you see the dew coming into the distillation head; then take the receiver off and close it tightly. Lute another receiver before it, well-fastened to the pipe of the distillation head. Distill until you perceive that the clear <term>water</term> <note>original: symbol $\nabla$</note> has come out. Then take this receiver, seal it with wax, and remove the distillation head from the vessel. It is clear and evident from experience that one should take neither the **Earth** <term>original: symbol ⊕; here referring to the solid matter or "body" of the grape</term> of the grapes, nor the wine directly from the press or the dregs, nor should one use the ash of the grapevines. All of these together contain evil humors <term>the four vital fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—which were believed to cause disease if unbalanced or impure</term>, which the wine casts off from itself before it becomes fit to drink. And those who wish to assist themselves with such works—who intend to make the **Water of Life** <term>original: aqua Vitæ; a highly refined medicinal spirit</term> or **Water of Life** <term>original: symbol ∇ Vitæ</term>—instead they make the **Water of Death** <term>original: symbol ∇ Mortis</term>. For they take an imperfect thing, which the nature of the wine casts off before it becomes fit to drink. It is as if a physician, wanting to purge evil humors, would take the foul, rotted matter he had just removed from one person through medicine and give it to another to drink, hoping to make that person healthy with it. So it is with those who hold such opinions regarding "foreign earths" <note>materials or minerals not naturally part of the refined wine</note>.

All the philosophers say this: one should make our **Stone** <note>the "Philosopher's Stone" or the supreme medicinal tincture</note> from one single thing, and never add anything foreign to it. Thus it is clear and true, for the reasons stated above, that one should take beautiful, clear wine and from it make the **Water of Life** <term>original: symbol ∇ Vitæ</term>, to preserve human life so that it might not be corrupted by the impurities of all kinds of humors until its final **limit** <note>original: Terminium; the natural allotted span of a human life</note>, and to properly return us to our original state of health.

I have given this reminder so that you may guard yourselves against taking up foreign earths and keep away from the ignorant, who might put other fantasies into your head and lead you away from the path of experience. You must always remain on the right path, without the error of what you call "foreign **water**" <term>original: symbol ∇</term>. In this way, you may prove yourselves and know how the nature of the foreign **water** <term>original: symbol ∇</term> should...

# On the Fifth [Essence]
<note>original title: De Quinta, referring to the "Quinta Essentia" or Quintessence—the fifth element that transcends the four physical elements.</note>

## On the Fifth [Operation]

Take the substance out of the receiver and pour it into the **fixing egg** <note>original: "figier Ei." An oval-shaped glass vessel used in alchemy for the prolonged heating and stabilization of a substance.</note>, and seal it with the **Seal of Hermes** <note>original: "Sigillo Hermetis." An airtight seal, often made by melting the glass neck of the vessel shut.</note>, and set it in **ashes** <term>original: "cineres"; a sand or ash bath used to provide even, indirect heat</term> deeper than the material sits. And give it the first 8 or 9 [days] a small **Fire** <term>original symbol: Δ</term>; the next 8 or 9 [days] increased, for the material begins to become coarse and to rise slowly. You should observe and note this: the material comes and rises from the bottom of the egg or glass up into the head of the egg and descends again. Then you shall see many **little veins** <note>Likely referring to "reflux" or streaks of condensation, often called the "tears" of the substance.</note> drawing themselves from the head of the egg and going down to the base; these veins shall be very many and innumerable because of their subtlety.

Now, however, the little streams shall become somewhat thicker or denser through that same rising and falling. When they now desire to become thick, they will appear less frequently than before, when they were very subtle; then you should make your **Fire** <term>original symbol: Δ</term> stronger, for your material desires to **fix** <note>To "fix" a substance means to transform it from a volatile, evaporating state into a solid or stable state that can withstand heat.</note>. For the thicker and coarser the little veins become, the fewer of them there will be; and the more fixed the material becomes, the better it can or may tolerate the **Fire** <term>original symbol: Δ</term>. And after this sign, you must make the **Fire** <term>original symbol: Δ</term> stronger, until you see that no more veins go up and down in the egg. Then you should hold the material for another 8 or 9 [days] in such heat, and then you will see another sign that the philosophers write of so wonderfully, and that is the sign of **Perfection**.

For Aristotle shows in *The Secret of Secrets* <note>original Latin: "De Secretis Secretorum." A famous medieval treatise attributed to Aristotle, covering alchemy, medicine, and statecraft.</note>, 15th Chapter: Our stone is the **Water** <term>original symbol: ∇</term> or the casting of the ice, and the instrument and hammer. [It is] body, tongs, or plane, with which the master works just as a blacksmith with the hammer will bring the forged work out according to his will; and it is struck with the hammer according to the master’s will.

# On the Fifth Essence of Wine

The King of Eternity, whose crown and mightiness He shall always retain, and therewith to the almighty eternal God for His holy gifts:

Now it is accomplished—God be praised beforehand—our Stone shall be made, say the <term>philosophers</term> <note>original: *philosophi*</note>, from one thing, without adding anything foreign, and it shall have within it the four elements. This will then be sufficiently taught and proven through understanding and discourse. Therefore says <term>Hermes</term> <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom many foundational alchemical texts are attributed.</note>: you should not open your purse if you wish to avoid expense; and <term>Arnold of Villanova</term> <note>A famous 13th-century physician and alchemist.</note> says in the *New Testament* <note>original: *Nova Testamento*. This refers not to the Bible, but to an alchemical treatise titled 'Novum Testamentum' attributed to Arnold of Villanova.</note>: God the Lord has given us two stones, one for the White and one for the Red: which we may have for free, as they grow, and one can have them whenever one wishes, and one needs to ask no one for permission. And he who knows this stone and can prepare it as before well, he needs no more to have expenses with the Art <note>The "Art" refers to Alchemy.</note>.

Therefore, keep well in your memory <note>original: *Memori*</note> what I have shown you here; I have opened the door for you and led you inside into the house of the <term>philosophers</term>, and led your small understanding to work, so you will see and understand wonderful things. And read this lesson several times before you begin to work, so that no defect may fall into your work: for I have told and written everything clearly to you, without any hidden words, and have taught you the way which I have handled with great care and labor. I have relieved you of your care and labor, arranged against all defects and errors that might encounter you in the work, without obscure words or with false intentions; also so that you, with clear understanding, may be content without loss of time. And if you have further understanding, you may understand much more from this report than I have written to you; for what one should do in the Art must all proceed upon one way and path, or one brings oneself into great expense, error, and fantasy, and will become a shame and a mockery before everyone.

<margin>v.</margin> **Calamine Stone** — calmey — <note>original: Lapis Calminaris; alchemical symbol: Z with crossbar. A zinc-rich mineral traditionally used in the making of brass.</note>

<margin>w.</margin> **Hematite** — Bloodstone <note>original: Lapis Hematitis or Blutstein; alchemical symbol: five vertical strokes. An iron oxide mineral used as a pigment and in medicine to stop bleeding.</note>

<margin>R.</margin> **Magnet** — <note>original: Magnet; alchemical symbol: S with horizontal crossbar. Also known as lodestone, valued for its magnetic properties.</note>

<margin>S.</margin> **Nitre** — Saltpeter — <note>original: Nitrum or Salpeter; alchemical symbol for Nitre: circle with horizontal bar. A key component in gunpowder and many chemical transformations.</note>

<margin>Z.</margin> **Common Salt** — <note>original: gemein Saltz; alchemical symbols: horizontal figure-eight and circle with horizontal bar. Sodium chloride, used in various purifying processes.</note>

<margin>V.</margin> **Common Salt or Rock Salt** — <note>original: Sal gemein oder Stein Saltz; alchemical symbols: horizontal figure-eight and circle with horizontal bar.</note>

<margin>DE.</margin> **Sal Ammoniac** — <note>original: Salmiac; alchemical symbol for Sal Ammoniac: X-shaped cross with terminal strokes. Ammonium chloride, used to dissolve metals and "open" minerals.</note>

<margin>ij.</margin> **Calcined Residue** — or **Dead Head** — <note>original: Calcator or Caput Mortuum; three alchemical symbols: a face/skull representing Caput Mortuum, a triangular funnel-like symbol, and a circle with internal letter 'T'. Caput Mortuum refers to the solid, often useless remains left in a vessel after a substance has been distilled or heated to exhaustion.</note>

<margin>Z.</margin> **or Salt of Calcination** <note>original: oder Sal Catoris; likely a reference to the salt extracted from the residue mentioned above.</note>

<margin>A.</margin> **Alkali Salt** — <note>original: Sal Alkali; alchemical symbol: horizontal figure-eight. A general term for salts derived from the ashes of plants.</note>

<margin>B.</margin> **Vitriolated Tartar** — <note>original: Tartarum Vitriolatum; alchemical symbols: symbol for Tartar and horizontal figure-eight. A chemical compound made by reacting salt of tartar with sulfuric acid, now known as potassium sulfate.</note>

<margin>C.</margin> **Salt of Tartar** — <note>original: Sal Tartari; alchemical symbol: circle with internal markings. Potassium carbonate, a strong alkaline substance derived from the sediment in wine barrels.</note>

<margin>D.</margin> **Calcined Tartar** — <note>original: Tartarus Calcinatus; alchemical symbol: circle with letter 'c' inside. Tartar that has been heated at high temperatures to achieve a high state of purity.</note>

E) **Tartar** <note>original: *Tartarus*; alchemical symbol: a cross over a horizontal line with a hook. This is the potassium bitartrate crust found in wine barrels, a staple reagent in alchemical purification.</note>

h) **Glass** <note>original: *Vitrum*; series of four alchemical symbols including an '8' shape, a 'b' shape, and a square arch. Glass was used both as a material for vessels and as a flux in metallurgical processes.</note>

i) **Urine** <note>original: *Vrina* (Latin) and *Harn* (German); two alchemical symbols: a square with a horizontal line and a stylized flower-like sun. Urine was a primary source of phosphorus and ammonia for early chemists.</note>

M)

h) **Burnt Alum** <note>original: *Gebrannten Alaun*; two alchemical symbols: a circle with a cross and a triangle with a vertical line. Alum that has been heated to drive off its water content, making it more concentrated and porous for use as a styptic or in dyeing.</note>

I) **Verdigris** <note>original: *Spangrien*; alchemical symbol: a circle with an internal cross. The green pigment formed by the action of acetic acid (vinegar) on copper; highly valued for its color and chemical reactivity.</note>

| <margin>K.</margin> | **Mary’s Bath** <term>AB.</term> <term>B: M.</term> <note>original: *Balneum Marae* (usually *Mariae*). Known today as a bain-marie or water bath, used to heat substances gently and evenly.</note> | <note>abbreviations: AB. and B: M. standing for *Aqua Balneum* and *Balneum Mariae*</note> |
| <margin>L.</margin> | **Vapor or Steam Bath** <note>original: *Vaporosum oder Dampffbad*. A method of heating using hot steam rather than direct water contact.</note> | <note>symbol: a 'V' shape</note> |
| <margin>M.<br>N.</margin> | **To Amalgamate** <note>original: *Almalgamieren*. The process of combining mercury with another metal to form an alloy or soft paste.</note> | <note>symbol: a hash or grid symbol and the abbreviation āāā, often standing for *amalgama*</note> |
| <margin>O.</margin> | **Layer upon Layer** <term>S: S: S:</term> <note>original: *Stratum Super Stratum*. A technique of alternating layers of different substances in a crucible to ensure even reaction.</note> | <note>abbreviation: S: S: S: for *Stratum Super Stratum*</note> |
| <margin>P.</margin> | **Fire Wheel or Circular Fire** <note>original: *Ignis Rota oder Circkel feuer*. A heating method where a fire is built in a ring around the outside of a vessel rather than beneath it.</note> | <note>symbol: a triangle (fire) enclosed within a circle</note> |
| <margin>Q.</margin> | **Sifted Stones** <note>original: *gesiebte steine*. Likely refers to crushed minerals or gravel used to pack furnaces or stabilize vessels.</note> | <note>symbol: a square</note> |
| <margin>R.</margin> | **Common Lute** <note>original: *Lutum Comūne*. A paste made of clay, horse manure, or sand used to seal joints in distillation equipment to prevent vapor from escaping.</note> | <note>symbol: a character resembling the digit 2</note> |
| <margin>S.<br>T.</margin> | **Crucible or Melting Pot** <term>T.</term> <note>original: *Crucibulum oder Schmelztiegl*. A vessel capable of withstanding very high temperatures, used for melting metals.</note> | <note>abbreviation: T. and a symbol depicting a vessel with a wide rim</note> |
| <margin>V.</margin> | **Ash** <term>E.</term> <note>original: *Asche*. Used as a source of potash or as a bedding material in sand baths.</note> | <note>abbreviation: E. and an Æ ligature symbol</note> |

## Yet Another
## Beautiful Key

**Gold** or **Sol** <note>original: *Soll*. *Sol* is the Latin name for the Sun, which alchemists associated with gold.</note> [Alchemical symbols for gold, including the standard solar circle with a center dot and a more complex calligraphic variant.]

**Luna** or **Silver** <note>original: *Silber*. *Luna* is the Latin name for the Moon, the celestial body corresponding to silver.</note> [Alchemical symbols for silver, including a crescent moon and a stylized variant.]

**Venus** or **Copper** <note>original: *Kupffer*. Venus is the planetary association for copper.</note> [Alchemical symbols for copper, including the standard Venus symbol, a variant with an additional crossbar, and the letters "Ze".]

<gloss>Saturn.</gloss> <note>original: *Saturnus*. Saturn is the planet traditionally associated with lead.</note>
**Jupiter** or **Lead** <note>original: *Bley*. Curiously, the scribe lists Jupiter here, though the symbols provided are for both Saturn and Jupiter. In alchemy, Saturn is almost universally the symbol for lead.</note> [Alchemical symbols for lead, featuring the symbols for both Saturn (♄) and Jupiter (♃), alongside the letters "L" and "b".]

**Jupiter** or **Tin** <note>original: *Zin*. Jupiter is the planetary association for tin.</note> [Alchemical symbols for tin, featuring the Jupiter symbol (♃), the Saturn symbol (♄), and a diamond-shaped geometric variant.]

**Mercury** or **Quicksilver** <note>original: *Mercuri / Quecksilber*. Mercury is the only metal that remains liquid at room temperature.</note> [Alchemical symbols for mercury, featuring four variants of the caduceus symbol (☿), ranging from standard to highly stylized.]

**Mars** or **Iron** <note>original: *Eisen*. Mars, the god of war, is the planetary association for iron, the metal of weaponry.</note> [Alchemical symbols for iron, featuring six variants of the Mars symbol (♂), including types with crosses and fork-like appendages.]

**Antimony** <note>original: *Antimoni*. A brittle, silvery-grey metalloid often used in the purification of gold.</note> [Alchemical symbols for antimony, featuring seven variants based on the globus cruciger (♁), including versions with nested squares and additional crosses.]

**Sulfur** or **Brimstone** <note>original: *Sulphur / Schwebl*. One of the three primary principles of alchemy (the Tria Prima), representing the soul and flammability.</note> [Alchemical symbols for sulfur, featuring eight variants based on the triangle-over-cross symbol (🜍), with several ornate calligraphic flourishes.]

**Saltpeter** <note>original: *Salpeter*. Also known as nitre; a key ingredient in gunpowder and various chemical "waters."</note> [Alchemical symbols for saltpeter, featuring eight variants including a circle with horizontal wavy lines (🜔), a crescent-and-circle icon, and other geometric patterns.]

**Verdigris** <note>original: *grüenspan*. The green pigment or crust that forms on copper; used in various chemical preparations.</note> [Alchemical symbols for verdigris, featuring five variants including a circle containing a cross and various triangular and curved forms.]

**Vitriol** <note>A term for a class of sulfate minerals (like copper or iron sulfate), often used to produce sulfuric acid.</note> [Alchemical symbols for vitriol, featuring five variants including the crossed-circle symbol (🜖), the Jupiter symbol, and the letters "L" and "q".]

**Tartar** <note>original: *Weinstein*. This is the potassium bitartrate crust found in wine barrels; alchemists used it as a flux and a source of "fixed" salt.</note> · [five alchemical symbols for tartar separated by dots]

**Cinnabar** <note>original: *Zinnober*. The bright red ore of mercury (mercury sulfide), essential for the "red" stage of the Great Work.</note> · [seven alchemical symbols for cinnabar, followed by a boxed symbol containing a cross and the number 333]

**Alum** <note>original: *Alaun*. An astringent mineral salt used as a mordant in dyeing and to "fix" other substances in alchemical recipes.</note> · [four alchemical symbols for alum]

**Sal Ammoniac** <note>original: *Salmiac*. Ammonium chloride, valued for its ability to sublimate and to help dissolve metals, particularly gold.</note> · [four alchemical symbols for sal ammoniac]

**Arsenic** <note>original: *Arsenicum*. Used by alchemists to "whiten" copper, simulating silver, though its toxicity was well-known.</note> · [series of ten symbols and notations for arsenic]

**Quicklime** <note>original: *Lebendiger Kalch*. Calcium oxide, produced by heating limestone. It "lives" because it reacts violently—generating heat—when touched by water.</note> · [seven alchemical symbols for quicklime]

**Litharge** <note>original: *Silberglöt*. A lead oxide formed as a byproduct of separating silver from lead ore.</note> · [four alchemical symbols for litharge]

**Orpiment** <note>original: *Auripigment*. An arsenic sulfide mineral named "gold pigment" because of its deep yellow color; it was often used in attempts to create gold.</note> · [five alchemical symbols for orpiment]

**Armenian Bole** <note>original: *Bolus Armeni*. A reddish-brown medicinal earth or clay used as a base in various chemical preparations.</note> · [abbreviation Ba. followed by an alchemical symbol]

**Brass** <note>original: *Messing*. An alloy of copper and zinc, often representing a "lesser" or false gold in early experiments.</note> · [three alchemical symbols for brass]

**Rock Salt** <note>original: *Sal gemme*. Naturally occurring halite or common salt crystals, distinguished from sea salt.</note> · [nine alchemical symbols for rock salt]

**Calamine** <note>original: *galmey*. A zinc ore; when heated with copper, it produces brass.</note> · [three alchemical symbols for calamine]

**Sublimated Mercury** <note>original: *Sublimierter Mercuri*. Quicksilver that has been heated into a vapor and collected as a purified solid, such as mercuric chloride.</note> · [three alchemical symbols for sublimated mercury]

**Mercury Precipitate** <note>original: *Mercuri Precipitat*. Mercury that has been forced out of a solution as a solid powder through chemical reaction.</note> · [three alchemical symbols for mercury precipitate]

**Other things that have been sublimated.** <note>original: *Andere Sachen so sublimiert seind.* A general category for any substance purified via sublimation (turning from solid to gas and back to solid).</note> · [three alchemical symbols, the last resembling the number 60]

**Precipitated things** <note>original: *Precipitierte Sachen*. General symbols for substances recovered from a liquid state as solids.</note> · [four alchemical symbols for precipitated substances]

**Mining or Ore** <note>original: *Bergwerck*. Literally "mountain-work," referring to the raw minerals as they are first extracted from the earth.</note> · [single alchemical symbol for mining/ore]

| **Gold Pyrites** <note>original: *gold Kies*. Also known as iron pyrites or "fool's gold," this mineral was often processed to extract sulfur or used in attempts to prove the presence of gold in "base" ores.</note> | A sequence consisting of a horizontal line with a hook, a sun symbol with rays and a face, a circle with a dot, and other alchemical glyphs. |
| **Garnets** <note>original: *granaten*. These deep red gemstones were sometimes ground for use in specific medicinal or alchemical preparations, associated with the "redness" of the philosopher's stone.</note> | An 'X' within a square and a square with internal lines and dots. |
| **Rock Salt** <note>original: *Stein Salz*. Natural halite. In the laboratory, salt was used to stabilize or "fix" volatile spirits, preventing them from escaping the heat of the furnace.</note> | A 'Z'-like character and a wavy horizontal line. |
| **Vitriol / Federweiß** <note>original: *fiedler*. This term often refers to fibrous minerals like asbestos or specific types of vitriol used for their heat-resistant properties.</note> | Two crescent moons with radial lines and two hooked cross symbols. |
| **Aqua Fortis** <note>original: *Aquafort.* Latin for "strong water" (nitric acid). This powerful acid was essential for parting gold from silver.</note> | A square symbol, the abbreviation 'Agf', the letter 'A.', and several triangular and cross-based alchemical variants. |
| **Vinegar** <note>original: *Essig*. Acetic acid, the primary solvent of the early laboratory, used to create "sugar of lead" and other metallic acetates.</note> | Two cross symbols with dots at the terminals of the arms. |
| **Distilled Vinegar** <note>original: *Distilierter Essig*. A purified and more potent form of vinegar, achieved through distillation to remove water and impurities.</note> | A crossed 'X' with dots and a symbol resembling the letters 'fto'. |
| **Wine** <note>original: *Wein*. The source of "spirit of wine" (ethanol) and tartar; it was viewed as a living substance containing a hidden celestial spirit.</note> | Crescent moons with rays, a horizontal line with an 'X', a '3X' notation, and a square with a hash symbol. |
| **Layer upon Layer** <note>original: *Stratum super Stratum*. A common laboratory instruction to alternate layers of different substances (like a metal and a salt) within a crucible.</note> | A cross and the repeated letters 'S S S'. |
| **Diligently** <note>original: *fleissig*. A frequent manual instruction urging the alchemist to perform a task—such as grinding or stirring—with great care or for a long duration.</note> | The lowercase abbreviation 'fl'. |
| **Hours** <note>original: *Stunden*. Time was a critical "ingredient" in alchemy; many processes required specific durations of heating to succeed.</note> | Hourglass-like symbols, an 'X', and a character with an 'St' superscript. |
| **Magnet** <note>original: *Magnet*. Lodestone. Alchemists studied magnetism as a visible proof of "sympathy," the hidden force that draws certain substances together.</note> | A Mars symbol (circle with an upward arrow) and a triangle with a tail. |
| **Fire** <note>original: *Feuer*. One of the four classical elements; represented by an upward triangle, signifying the upward motion of heat and flame.</note> | An upward-pointing triangle (Δ) and a cursive glyph. |
| **Water** <note>original: *Wasser*. One of the four classical elements; represented by a downward triangle, signifying the nature of liquid to flow downward.</note> | A downward-pointing triangle (∇) and a horizontal wavy line. |
| **Air** <note>original: *Lufft*. One of the four classical elements; an upward triangle with a bar, representing the "levity" of the atmosphere.</note> | An upward-pointing triangle with a horizontal bar. |
| **Earth** <note>original: *Erden*. One of the four classical elements; a downward triangle with a bar, representing the "gravity" and density of solid matter.</note> | A downward-pointing triangle with a horizontal bar. |
| **Earth** <note>The repetition of the entry for Earth likely indicates different variations of the symbol used in different manuscript traditions.</note> | A downward-pointing triangle with a horizontal bar and internal line decoration. |
| **Day** <note>original: *Tag*. Often used to indicate the length of a "digestion" process, where a substance was kept in gentle heat for several days.</note> | Characters resembling a cursive '6' and 'd'. |

| **Flux / To Flow** <note>original: *Fließen*. This likely refers to the process of melting or a "fluxing" agent added to minerals to lower their melting point. | **Amalgam** <note>original: *Amalgama*. An alloy formed by mixing mercury with another metal, such as gold or silver. This was a critical step in both mining and the "transmutation" of metals.</note> | Three variants of alchemical symbols for amalgam, including "aa" and "aaa" <note>the standard abbreviation for *amalgama*</note>. |
| **Crucible** <note>original: *Tegl*. A heat-resistant ceramic or graphite container used for melting metals or performing high-temperature chemical reactions.</note> | Three variants of a cup-shaped symbol representing a crucible. |
| **Calcined Tartar** <note>original: *Calcionierter Weinstein*. Tartar is the potassium bitartrate residue from wine barrels. When "calcined" (burned to ash), it produces potassium carbonate, a strong alkali used as a solvent.</note> | Four variants of alchemical symbols for calcined tartar, featuring crosses and semi-circles. |
| **Marcasite** <note>original: *Marcasit* / *March'*. A brittle, pale bronze-yellow iron sulfide. Early chemists often used this term broadly for various metallic sulfides and ores.</note> | Three variants of symbols for marcasite, including a square with an internal cross, and two variants consisting of the letter 'm' with signs above. |

| **Manual / Tool** <note>original: *Manals*. Likely referring to a *manuale*, a hand-held tool or a specific measuring vessel used in the furnace room.</note> | A square symbol with an internal cross. |
| **Cupel** <note>original: *Treibscherumb*. A small, porous bowl made of bone ash. It was used in "cupellation" to separate precious metals from lead; the lead oxidizes and is absorbed into the cupel, leaving a bead of pure gold or silver behind.</note> | A circle with a central dot representing a cupel. |
| **Potash** <note>original: *Pot asche*. An alkaline salt (potassium carbonate) obtained by leaching wood ashes in a pot. It was a fundamental ingredient in making glass and soap.</note> | An alchemical symbol for potash resembling a cross over a crescent or cup. |
| **Quintessence** <note>original: *Quinta Essentia*. Literally the "fifth essence." In alchemy, this was the purest, most concentrated medicinal force extracted from a substance, believed to be the celestial element of the terrestrial world.</note> | Two alchemical symbols for the fifth essence, including the abbreviation "Q:E:". |
| **Realgar** <note>original: *Realgar*. A bright red arsenic sulfide mineral. It was highly toxic and used for its arsenic content and its vivid color.</note> | Three variants of the alchemical symbol for realgar. |
| **Alkali Salt** <note>original: *Sal Alkali*. A general term for water-soluble salts like potash or soda. These were essential for neutralizing acids or acting as fluxes in metallurgy.</note> | Two variants of the symbol for alkali salt. |
| **Tufa** <note>original: *Tuffstein*. A porous volcanic rock. In alchemy, such stones were sometimes used for filtration or as a source of earthy minerals.</note> | A rectangular symbol with a central horizontal line. |
| **Soap** <note>original: *Seiffe*. Beyond hygiene, soap was used in the laboratory as a lubricant, a binder for certain pastes, or for cleaning metallic surfaces.</note> | A diamond or lozenge symbol. |
| **Slag / Scoria** <note>original: *Schlaggerr*. The stony waste matter separated from metals during the smelting or refining of ore.</note> | An alchemical symbol for slag or scoria. |
| **Brick** <note>original: *Zieglstein*. Bricks were used to construct furnaces. In powdered form (brick dust), they served as a "lute" or sealant for joints in glass apparatus.</note> | A rectangle with diagonal hatching representing a brick. |
| **Glass-gall** <note>original: *glaßgalle*. Also known as sandiver. This is the layer of impurities and salts that floats to the top of molten glass during manufacture.</note> | A circle containing a cross representing glass-gall. |
| **Brick Dust** <note>original: *Zieglmehl*. Finely ground brick, often used as a mild abrasive or mixed with egg whites and clay to seal laboratory vessels.</note> | A rectangle filled with dots representing brick dust. |
| **Wick** <note>original: *Doch*. The wick used in oil lamps or candles, which provided the low, steady heat required for long-term "digestion" or incubation of chemical mixtures.</note> | A stylized symbol resembling a ligature of the letters "mo". |

# Shapes of various distillation vessels
<note>original: *Distilier glößer*. In the early modern period, glass was the preferred material for these processes because it allowed the operator to see changes in color and state, and it did not react with most acids.</note>

- Row 2 (8-13): Shows "philosophical eggs" (8-9), a vial (10), a chalice-like separating glass (11), a blind helm (12), and a large receiver (13) resting on a circular base.
- Row 3 (14-16): Includes a pear-shaped flask (14), a retort (15) on a base, and a cucurbit (16).
Item 17 (the straw ring base) is shown supporting vessels 13 and 15.

# Physical Features: The Book’s Binding

## The Tooled Leather Cover

->**Decorative Blind-Tooling**<-

The photograph reveals a large, closed manuscript bound in dark brown leather. The binding is a primary example of **blind-tooling** <term>blind-tooling<note>A decorative technique where patterns are impressed into the leather using heated metal stamps or rollers without the application of gold leaf or ink.</note></term>. The layout of the decoration is highly structured, featuring a repeating floral border that frames the outer edges of the cover.

In the center, a complex geometric design takes prominence. A large "X" pattern creates a central diamond motif, within which four smaller diamonds are stamped with intricate decorative flourishes. This type of geometric symmetry was a hallmark of European bookbinding during the late medieval and early modern periods.

On the right side of the volume, the deep red staining of the page edges—noted in previous descriptions—is clearly visible, creating a sharp contrast against the dark leather. The book also retains remnants of its original **clasps** <term>clasps<note>Functional fasteners consisting of leather straps and metal components. These were essential for large volumes to keep the covers tightly shut, preventing the paper or parchment from warping due to changes in humidity.</note></term>. One leather strap remains attached to the fore-edge of the back cover, while another fragment hangs from the bottom edge, providing a tactile sense of the book’s history and its life as a protected object in a library.

<header>The Splendor of the Sun.</header>
<meta>MC.</meta>

## The Third Manifestation.

<note>original: "drittlegebarung." This refers to the third stage or "parable" in the alchemical process described in this text.</note>

As it is to be understood in the chapter on the **Earth of Man**, who purifies himself in the mire in which he was found, and sets aside all impurities that naturally cling to him, and transforms the entire nature that is within man into a heavenly and clear **matter** <note>original: "Materia"; the physical substance being transformed</note>; just as <term>Hermes</term> <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure regarded as the founder of alchemy</note> says in his fourth book: "I have seen three birds flying through the air, and afterwards they settled down; one was white, the other black, and the third was red." This is to be understood thus: the black is the head, the white is the breast, and the red are the feet. And so it is a perfect work, for in this third manifestation, the **Earth**—which is the **Body**—is purified of all other impurities, and the clarity of the **Soul** reveals itself, and it mingles with the **Spirit**, working a heavenly substance, so that they never separate from one another thereafter. For all three are one, in one form and in one person, and all three together appear shining and clear, like the sun. Thus, a perfect work emerges from the **clump of earth** <note>original: "Erdtklumpen"</note> which was once considered an impurity. This treasure was revealed by God to those three wise men, whom we now have and must hear, so that you do not think so strangely of this; for it is such a great mystery which God previously revealed to the wise, so that they might banish their poverty and praise God for sharing such grace with them, to demonstrate His wondrousness through this, with an infinite wealth and the blessing of a perfect life.

<meta>catchword: 7. Figure.</meta>

<summary>This page describes the "Third Manifestation" of the alchemical process, using the allegory of three birds (black, white, and red) to symbolize the purification and unification of body, soul, and spirit into a "heavenly substance." It emphasizes that the highest treasure is found by refining what was once considered lowly "mire" or "clumps of earth."</summary>
<keywords>Splendor Solis, alchemy, Hermes Trismegistus, purification, Three Birds, body soul and spirit, transmutation, Great Work, alchemy of man</keywords>
